If any constant has a different name in the source (e.g., PRODUCT_TITLE instead of PRODUCT_NAME), the wrapper exits with AttributeError, the bridge surfaces it as type: "source_error", and the operator sees a misleading "fix curriculum.py" message when the real problem is a hallucinated attribute name. This table prevents that by requiring explicit verification.

7.2 Subprocess-dispatched API routes

?src=live dispatch rule (explicit branching rule): For GET /api/packs/:slug/html and GET /api/packs/:slug/pdf, the bridge inspects the src query parameter before any subprocess or file operation begins:

  1. If src is present and equals live (exact match, case-sensitive): dispatch to the subprocess wrapper (render-pack-html or render-pack-pdf). The response is freshly rendered from current source.
  2. Otherwise (no src parameter, or src is any value other than live — including src=committed or src=anything-else): serve committed bytes from site/packs/{slug}.html or site/packs/pdf/{slug}.pdf via direct file I/O (§7.3). No subprocess is spawned.

This dispatch is implemented as a single handler per path that inspects urllib.parse.parse_qs(...).get('src') and branches — not as two independent route registrations. An implementer who registers two independent routes risks missing the dispatch; the single-handler approach is mandatory.

Method & PathWrapper commandReturns
GET /api/curriculumcurriculumFull curriculum tree, snake_case keys exactly as authored in Python
GET /api/statusstatusAggregate: module/pack counts, per-pack freshness, config state, bundle readiness, last build/test from console-state.json
GET /api/packspacksSeven-pack inventory: slug, band, module title, file sizes, mtimes, freshness flags
POST /api/buildAcquire build lock → build (120s timeout) → release lock → atomically update console-state.json{ ok: true, data: BuildResult } where BuildResult.ok is true on success or false on build failure. On build failure, BuildResult includes error, type: "build_failure", and best-effort artifacts/zips arrays from a filesystem scan after the subprocess exits (§5.14). On timeout: { ok: false, error, type: "timeout" }. On lock contention: HTTP 409 with { ok: false, error, type: "lock_contention" }. On source error: { ok: false, error, type: "source_error" }.
POST /api/testAcquire build lock → test (120s timeout) → release lock → atomically update console-state.json{ ok: true, data: TestResult } where TestResult.ok is true if all tests passed. Failures are represented inside TestResult (passed/failed/errors counts, per-failure detail). On timeout: { ok: false, error, type: "timeout" }. On lock contention: HTTP 409 with type: "lock_contention".
GET /api/packs/:slug/html?src=liverender-pack-html <module_id> <band_key> (30s)text/html — what current source would produce; visual diff against committed bytes. Serves the wrapper's HTML string as the response body. On subprocess failure: returns text/html HTTP 200 with the HTML error page (§7.2a) so the iframe displays a readable error instead of raw JSON.
GET /api/packs/:slug/pdf?src=liverender-pack-pdf <module_id> <band_key> (30s) → temp file (delete=False)application/pdf bytes from current source; bridge serves the temp file then deletes it with os.unlink() in a finally block. On subprocess failure: returns text/html HTTP 200 with the HTML error page (§7.2a) — an iframe navigated to a text/html response renders it, so the error appears in place of the PDF (§5.13).
GET /api/tools/:toolIdrender-tool-html <tool_id> (30s)text/html minimal document wrapping the fragment (§7.6). 404 with JSON if tool_id not found. On subprocess failure: returns text/html HTTP 200 with the HTML error page (§7.2a).
7.2a HTML error page for failed live renders

When a live-render subprocess exits non-zero or times out — for any failure type (SyntaxError, IndentationError, NameError, RuntimeError, MemoryError, timeout, import failure, or any other exception) — the bridge returns an HTML error page instead of a JSON envelope, so iframes display a readable message. The error message is HTML-escaped on the bridge side using Python's html.escape() function from the standard library before insertion into the template. html.escape(error_message, quote=True) converts & → &amp;, < → &lt;, > → &gt;, " → &quot;, and ' → &#x27; — preventing any error text containing <script>…</script> or other HTML markup from executing in the iframe context, even in a loopback-only tool. The escaping is performed bridge-side, in the bridge's error-handling code, before the HTML string is assembled:

import html

def build_error_page(error_message: str, context_hint: str = "content/curriculum.py") -> str:
    escaped = html.escape(error_message, quote=True)
    escaped_hint = html.escape(context_hint, quote=True)
    return f"""<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>Preview Error</title>
  <style>
    body {{ margin: 24px; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif;
           color: #1a1a22; background: #fafafa; }}
    .error {{ padding: 16px; border: 1px solid #dc2626; border-radius: 8px;
             background: #fef2f2; max-width: 600px; }}
    .error h2 {{ color: #dc2626; margin: 0 0 8px 0; font-size: 16px; }}
    .error p {{ margin: 4px 0; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.5; }}
    .error code {{ font-family: monospace; font-size: 13px;
                  background: #fee2e2; padding: 2px 6px; border-radius: 3px; }}
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <div class="error">
    <h2>Preview Error</h2>
    <p>Could not render this pack from current source.</p>
    <p><strong>Error:</strong> <code>{escaped}</code></p>
    <p>Check <code>{escaped_hint}</code> for errors, then try again.</p>
  </div>
</body>
</html>"""

The response carries Content-Type: text/html and HTTP 200 so the iframe renders it as a page, not a download or an error. This applies uniformly to all three live-render routes — pack HTML, pack PDF, and tool preview — and to all failure modes (syntax errors, runtime errors, timeouts).

7.3 Direct file-I/O API routes and special endpoints
Method & PathBridge actionReturns
GET /api/packs/:slug/htmlServe committed bytes of site/packs/:slug.html read fresh from disk on every request (path-confined; slug validated against the known-slug set enumerated from all_module_band_pairs() + pack_slug()). Dispatch rule: if ?src=live is present, route to the subprocess handler (§7.2) instead.text/html — the deliverable as customers receive it (iframe source). 404 with JSON if missing.
GET /api/packs/:slug/pdfServe committed bytes of site/packs/pdf/:slug.pdf read fresh from disk on every request. Dispatch rule: if ?src=live is present, route to the subprocess handler (§7.2) instead.application/pdf bytes. 404 with JSON if missing.
GET /api/configRead and parse site/assets/config.js using the extraction and parsing logic in §7.4{ checkoutUrl, contactEmail, checkoutConfigured }, or { ok: false, error: "config.js is malformed: <detail>", type: "config_corrupted" } if the file is missing or unparseable (§7.4)
PUT /api/configValidate inputs, rewrite site/assets/config.js from the fixed template with escaped values (§7.4){ ok, checkoutUrl, contactEmail } or { ok: false, errors: [{field, message}] }
GET /api/pilotRead console/data/pilot-state.json; initialize defaults if absent; inject thresholds from the bridge's static config block (§7.5a) into the responseFull pilot state including _version and thresholds (§7.5a). If the file exists but is corrupted: { ok: false, error: "pilot-state.json is corrupted", type: "pilot_corrupted" } (§13 recovery path)
PUT /api/pilotValidate _version against the stored version (optimistic concurrency, §7.5); strip thresholds from the request body before any storage; normalize all email addresses (trim + lowercase) on the server before storage and comparison; if version match, write the new state atomically with incremented _version; if mismatch, return 409Saved pilot state (with new _version and thresholds injected) on success. HTTP 409 with { ok: false, error: "Pilot data was modified in another session. The latest version has been loaded.", type: "pilot_version_conflict", data: <current stored state with thresholds injected> } on version conflict.
POST /api/pilot/resetBypass the optimistic-concurrency check entirely (no _version required in the request body, no version check performed); call os.makedirs('console/data', exist_ok=True); write the §6.4 default object atomically (temp file + os.replace) with _version: 0. Does not touch console/data/console-state.json or any product file.{ ok: true, data: <default pilot state with thresholds injected> }. This endpoint exists specifically because a PUT /api/pilot with _version: 0 would be rejected by the concurrency guard whenever the stored version is greater than 0 — which is almost always the case after any pilot activity. Reset is an intentional, double-confirmed operator act with its own endpoint, not a PUT with a special flag.
GET /api/packagingRead packaging.jsonFull packaging metadata
GET /OPERATOR_GUIDE.mdStatic file read from repo rootRaw markdown text

Static file routes (read-only, same origin, path-confined per §6.6): GET /site/ → site/ directory (customer site preview); GET /artifacts/ → project-root dist/ (zip bundle downloads); GET / and unmatched non-API paths → SPA per §6.5.

7.4 Config template, escaping, validation, parsing, and corruption handling

Config file parsing — robust extraction with raw_decode. The bridge reads site/assets/config.js and extracts the window.LSF_CONFIG = { ... }; assignment. The parser must handle braces inside JSON string values (e.g., a checkout URL containing }) and braces in comments before the assignment. The naive content.find('}') approach is prohibited because it finds the first } character, not the matching brace — a URL like https://example.com/callback?data={token} would truncate the extraction, causing json.loads to fail and the bridge to report config_corrupted on a file it just wrote.

The corrected parser uses json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode(), which parses a JSON object starting from a given position, correctly handling braces inside string literals:

def parse_config(content: str) -> dict:
    """Extract and parse the window.LSF_CONFIG object from config.js.

    Uses raw_decode to handle braces inside JSON string values (e.g., URLs
    with query parameters containing '}'). This is critical: a naive
    find('}') would truncate extraction at the first '}' inside a string,
    causing false config_corrupted errors on valid files.
    """
    marker = 'window.LSF_CONFIG'
    start = content.find(marker)
    if start == -1:
        raise ValueError("window.LSF_CONFIG not found")
    # Find the '=' after the marker, then the first '{' at or after it.
    # This skips any braces in comments between the marker and the assignment.
    eq_pos = content.find('=', start)
    if eq_pos == -1:
        raise ValueError("Expected '=' after window.LSF_CONFIG")
    brace_start = content.find('{', eq_pos)
    if brace_start == -1:
        raise ValueError("Expected '{' after window.LSF_CONFIG =")
    # raw_decode parses one JSON value from the starting position,
    # consuming exactly the object (including nested braces in strings).
    decoder = json.JSONDecoder()
    obj, end_offset = decoder.raw_decode(content[brace_start:])
    return obj

Why raw_decode instead of a brace counter: raw_decode is a stdlib function that implements a full JSON parser, handling string literals, escape sequences, and nested structures. A manual brace counter must also track string state (in-string vs. outside), escape sequences (\", \\), and nested objects — all of which raw_decode already handles correctly. Using raw_decode is both safer and shorter than a hand-rolled counter.

Why find = before {: If the operator hand-edits the file and adds a comment containing { between window.LSF_CONFIG and the = sign (e.g., // Config { version: 2 }), searching for { from the marker position finds the brace in the comment. Searching for = first, then { after the =, skips comment braces that appear before the assignment. This is robust for the template's documented comment format; a comment containing = followed by { on the same line before the real assignment would still break it, but that pattern is implausible for a hand-editing operator and the template's own comments never contain {.

Config file writing — template with quoted keys. The bridge writes site/assets/config.js from this exact template, using {{ and }} to produce literal braces in Python's str.format():

CONFIG_TEMPLATE = """// Life Skills Foundations — Checkout Configuration
// Generated by Pilot Deck console (PUT /api/config).
// WARNING: saving from the console regenerates this ENTIRE file.
// Hand-edits, custom comments, and extra fields will be OVERWRITTEN.
window.LSF_CONFIG = {{
  "checkoutUrl": {checkout_json},
  "contactEmail": {email_json}
}};
"""

def js_safe(s: str) -> str:
    """JSON-encode, then escape angle brackets for script-tag context."""
    return json.dumps(s).replace('<', '\\u003c').replace('>', '\\u003e')

content = CONFIG_TEMPLATE.format(
    checkout_json=js_safe(checkout_url),
    email_json=js_safe(contact_email),
)

This produces:

window.LSF_CONFIG = {
  "checkoutUrl": "https://example.com",
  "contactEmail": "test@example.com"
};

The keys "checkoutUrl" and "contactEmail" are double-quoted, making the object valid JSON as well as valid JavaScript. json.loads() on the extracted { "checkoutUrl": "…", "contactEmail": "…" } succeeds. Unquoted JavaScript keys (checkoutUrl:) would be valid JS but invalid JSON — json.loads() would raise JSONDecodeError, causing the bridge's own read endpoint to report config_corrupted on a file the bridge's own write endpoint just created. Quoted keys keep the round-trip sound. This quoting is unconditional — it always applies regardless of input values.

Escaping rationale: json.dumps escapes quotes, backslashes, and control characters, preventing breakout from the JS string literal. The additional < → \u003c and > → \u003e replacement turns any </script> in the value into \u003c/script\u003e, which cannot close the HTML script tag when the file is loaded via <script src="assets/config.js">. This is the standard defense for JSON-in-HTML.

Validation (enforced before write; rejected writes leave the file untouched):

  • checkoutUrl: empty string OR starts with https://. Additionally, the raw value must not contain the substring </script (case-insensitive) — belt-and-suspenders behind the escaping.
  • contactEmail: empty string OR matches ^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$. The placeholder pilot@example.com is allowed but triggers an amber UI note.

Corruption handling: if GET /api/config finds the file missing or unparseable — for any reason (missing window.LSF_CONFIG marker, missing =, missing {, invalid JSON, truncated file, non-text content) — it returns { ok: false, error: "config.js is malformed: <detail>", type: "config_corrupted" }. The Dashboard shows a red Alert; the Launch screen disables the form fields, shows the red Alert — "config.js could not be parsed. The file may have been hand-edited with a syntax error." — and offers a "Reset to defaults" button that calls PUT /api/config with empty strings, regenerating a valid file from the template. The corruption detection is based on a genuine parse attempt using raw_decode, not pattern matching against known-bad strings.

7.5 Pilot state defaults, concurrency, server-side normalization, and corruption

Defaults are the exact object in §6.4 (with _version: 0, and no thresholds field — thresholds are injected by the bridge on GET, never persisted to disk). If console/data/pilot-state.json exists but cannot be parsed — for any reason (truncated JSON, non-text binary content, valid JSON lacking expected keys, missing closing brace, trailing garbage) — GET /api/pilot returns { ok: false, ..., type: "pilot_corrupted" }; the Pilot screen shows a red Alert — "Pilot state file is corrupted. You can reset it to defaults; previous entries will be lost." — with a "Reset pilot data" button that calls POST /api/pilot/reset (the dedicated reset endpoint, §7.3), which writes the default object with _version: 0 without checking the stored version. The bridge never silently discards a corrupted file; reset is an explicit operator act.

Server-side email normalization (binding): The bridge must normalize all email addresses received via PUT /api/pilot by trimming whitespace and converting to lowercase before storage and comparison. This is a server-side requirement, not a client-side convenience: a direct API call (e.g., curl) that sends " Jane@Example.COM " must result in the stored value "jane@example.com". Client-side normalization is insufficient because it does not protect against direct API calls that bypass the UI. The bridge normalizes each sale.email in the incoming sales array before any storage or duplicate check.

Thresholds stripping (binding): The bridge must strip the thresholds field from the PUT request body before writing to pilot-state.json. Thresholds are never persisted to disk. On every GET /api/pilot response, the bridge always injects thresholds from its static config block (§7.5a), ignoring any thresholds field that may exist in the file. This prevents stale thresholds from surviving a B10 reconciliation — exactly the drift §7.5a was designed to prevent.

Concurrency control on PUT /api/pilot: the request body must include _version matching the currently stored value. The bridge compares body._version to stored._version:

  • Match: write the new state atomically (temp file + os.replace), with _version set to stored._version + 1, and return { ok: true, data: <new state with updated _version and thresholds injected> }.
  • Mismatch: return HTTP 409 with { ok: false, error: "Pilot data was modified in another session. The latest version has been loaded.", type: "pilot_version_conflict", data: <current stored state with thresholds injected> }. No write occurs.

The client handles the 409 by opening the VersionConflictDialog (§10.7): "This pilot data was updated in another tab. The latest version has been loaded, including [N] sales entries. Please review your changes and re-enter them." The dialog reads the current state from the response's data field (no second round-trip needed to display it), the client invalidates the ['pilot'] query to sync its cache, and the operator re-enters their changes against the fresh _version.

This is sufficient for a single-user, occasional-tab scenario. The operator is one person; concurrent saves are accidental (forgotten tab), not adversarial.

7.5a Pilot threshold metadata in API response

Pilot thresholds are exposed to the client via the GET /api/pilot response to prevent client/bridge drift. The thresholds live in a static config block inside the bridge (§8.2). Without exposing them, the React client would have to hardcode the same values — creating a drift hazard if the B10 artifact is reconciled and the bridge updates its static block while the client displays stale thresholds.

The GET /api/pilot response includes a thresholds array alongside the pilot state. The bridge always injects this array from its static config block — it is never read from the pilot-state.json file on disk:

The thresholds array is never persisted to pilot-state.json. On PUT /api/pilot, the bridge strips the thresholds field from the request body before writing to disk. On GET /api/pilot, the bridge always injects thresholds from its static config block into the response, ignoring any thresholds field that may exist in the file. This ensures threshold values are always current with the bridge's compiled-in config and never drift from stale file content if the B10 artifact is reconciled and the bridge is updated. The ChannelCard components render from this array — never from hardcoded client constants. The PilotState TypeScript type (§8) includes a thresholds: ThresholdMeta[] field. The bridge is the single source of truth for threshold values; the client is data-driven.

7.6 Tool preview wrapping

The wrapper calls render_tool_html(tool_id) (listed in the Backend Artifact Manifest under tools/render_html.py). The bridge inspects the returned string: if it begins with <!DOCTYPE or <html (case-insensitive) it is served as-is; otherwise the bridge wraps the fragment. Wrapping is the bridge's responsibility, not the render function's. On subprocess failure — for any failure type — the bridge returns the HTML error page (§7.2a), not JSON, because this route serves an iframe.

<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
  <meta charset="utf-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
  <title>Tool Preview: {tool_id}</title>
  <style>
    body { margin: 24px; font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, sans-serif;
           color: #1a1a22; background: #fafafa; max-width: 680px; }
    @media print { @page { size: Letter; margin: 0.75in; } }
  </style>
</head>
<body>{fragment}</body>
</html>
7.7 Test result parsing (no regex on human-readable output, stdout fully captured)

The test wrapper command uses unittest's programmatic API and prints structured JSON. Critically, the entire stdout stream must be captured via contextlib.redirect_stdout into a StringIO before the suite runs — not just the TextTestRunner's stream, but the global sys.stdout. Without this, any print statement in the 48 existing tests or in content/curriculum.py (which is imported during test discovery) writes to the real sys.stdout, corrupting the JSON envelope on the wrapper's stdout pipe. The build wrapper already does this (§6.3); the test wrapper must do the same.

import unittest, json, io, sys, contextlib

# Redirect ALL stdout (not just the runner's stream) into StringIO.
# Any print() in test code or imported modules would otherwise corrupt
# the JSON envelope on stdout.
output_buffer = io.StringIO()

with contextlib.redirect_stdout(output_buffer):
    loader = unittest.TestLoader()
    suite = loader.discover('tests', top_level_dir='.')
    runner = unittest.TextTestRunner(verbosity=2, stream=output_buffer)
    result = runner.run(suite)

# Now write only the structured JSON to the real stdout
captured_output = output_buffer.getvalue()

failures_detail = []
for test, tb in result.failures:
    failures_detail.append({"name": str(test), "type": "failure", "traceback": tb})
for test, tb in result.errors:
    failures_detail.append({"name": str(test), "type": "error", "traceback": tb})

sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
    "total": result.testsRun,
    "passed": result.testsRun - len(result.failures) - len(result.errors),
    "failed": len(result.failures),
    "errors": len(result.errors),
    "ok": result.wasSuccessful(),
    "failures": failures_detail,
    "stdout": captured_output,
}))

The bridge wraps this JSON in the standard envelope. Contract-validation badges (§10.5) are derived from these per-test names — never from re-implemented logic.

7.8 Removed endpoints

POST /api/build/html and POST /api/build/pdf do not exist (§5.10). Requests to them return 404. Only full build (POST /api/build) and POST /api/test are exposed.

7.9 Functions explicitly not surfaced

test_discount_applies(), test_rejects_negative(), main() in skill verify scripts, require_auth() — these live under .claude/skills/ as skill examples, not product surfaces. est_width, wrap_text, esc, PDF, Canvas, Flow are internal rendering machinery, not operator entry points.

8. TypeScript Data Model

These types mirror the Python dicts defined by _lesson() and TOOLS in content/curriculum.py. The bridge serializes curriculum data exactly as Python structures; keys remain snake_case to match the source.

// src/types/index.ts

export type AgeBandKey = "5-8" | "9-12";

export interface Lesson {
  week: number;
  title: string;
  minutes: number;
  materials: string[];
  say: string[];
  demonstrate: string[];
  practice: { task: string; done_when: string };
  wrap_up?: string;
}

export interface Band {
  lessons: Lesson[];
  tools: string[];      // keys into TOOLS
  checklist: string[];
}

export interface Module {
  id: string;
  number: number;
  title: string;
  domain: string;
  tagline: string;
  parent_intro: string;
  bands: Record<AgeBandKey, Band>;
}

export interface Tool {
  id: string;
  kind: string;
  title: string;
  variant?: string;
  instructions?: string;
  lines?: string[];
  chore_rows?: number;
  with_share?: boolean;
  goal_line?: boolean;
  rows?: number;
  serves?: string;
  time?: string;
  ingredients?: string[];
  steps?: string[];
  days_prefilled?: number;
  days_total?: number;
  body?: string;
  fields?: string[];
}

export interface ProductMeta {
  name: string;
  subtitle: string;
  price_usd: number;
  guarantee_days: number;
}

export interface CurriculumData {
  meta: ProductMeta;
  modules: Module[];
  tools: Record<string, Tool>;
  band_labels: Record<AgeBandKey, string>;
}

export type PackFreshness = "fresh" | "stale" | "missing";

export interface PackSummary {
  slug: string;
  module_id: string;
  module_title: string;
  band_key: AgeBandKey;
  band_label: string;
  html_exists: boolean;
  pdf_exists: boolean;
  html_size: number;
  pdf_size: number;
  html_modified: string;
  pdf_modified: string;
  status: PackFreshness;   // §6.7 mtime comparison against all source files
}

export interface BuildResult {
  ok: boolean;             // false if the build itself failed
  log: string;
  artifacts: PackSummary[]; // best-effort snapshot; present even when ok is false
  zips: ZipBundle[];        // best-effort snapshot; present even when ok is false
  duration_ms: number;
  completed_at: string;
  error?: string;          // present when ok is false
  type?: string;           // present when ok is false ("build_failure", "source_error")
}

export interface ZipBundle {
  name: string;
  path: string;
  size: number;
  exists: boolean;
}

export interface TestFailureDetail {
  name: string;
  type: "failure" | "error";
  traceback: string;
}

export interface TestResult {
  ok: boolean;
  passed: number;
  failed: number;
  errors: number;
  total: number;
  duration_ms: number;
  failures: TestFailureDetail[];
  stdout: string;
}

export interface ConfigState {
  checkoutUrl: string;
  contactEmail: string;
  checkoutConfigured: boolean;
}

export type ChannelKey =
  | "community"
  | "partnerships"
  | "content"
  | "paid_social"
  | "organic_referral";

export interface ThresholdMeta {
  experiment_id: string;
  channel: string;
  channel_key: ChannelKey;
  success_threshold: number;
  kill_threshold: number | null;
  budget_usd: number;
  duration_days: number;
}

export interface SaleEntry {
  id: string;
  email: string;
  channel: ChannelKey;
  date: string;             // ISO date
}

export interface KillAcknowledgment {
  acknowledged_at: string;  // ISO date
  stopped_tracking: boolean;
}

export interface PilotState {
  _version: number;         // managed by bridge; client sends last-read value on PUT
  launch_date: string | null;
  target_families: number;
  target_feedback: number;
  sales: SaleEntry[];
  feedback_count: number;
  acceptance_checklist: {
    purchasers_40: boolean;
    checkout_autonomous: boolean;
    reports_20: boolean;
    reports_genuine: boolean;
  };
  kill_acknowledgments: Record<string, KillAcknowledgment>;
  thresholds: ThresholdMeta[];  // injected by bridge on GET, stripped on PUT; never persisted to disk
}

export type ChannelStatus =
  | "on_track" | "warning" | "kill" | "killed" | "passed" | "failed";

export interface ChannelThreshold {
  experiment_id: string;        // "E-001" … "E-005"
  channel: string;              // display name
  channel_key: ChannelKey;
  success_threshold: number;
  kill_threshold: number | null; // null for organic
  budget_usd: number;
  duration_days: number;
  current_count: number;         // sales in window for this channel
  days_elapsed: number;
  status: ChannelStatus;
  acknowledged: boolean;
  stopped_tracking: boolean;
  window_start: string | null;   // launch_date
  window_end: string | null;     // launch_date + duration_days
}

export interface StatusResponse {
  module_count: number;
  pack_count: number;
  packs: PackSummary[];
  config: ConfigState | null;
  config_error: string | null;   // non-null when config.js is corrupted
  zips: ZipBundle[];
  last_build: { completed_at: string; ok: boolean; duration_ms: number } | null;
  last_test: { passed: number; failed: number; completed_at: string } | null;
}

export type BridgeResponse<T> =
  | { ok: true; data: T }
  | { ok: false; error: string; type?: string; data?: T }; // data present for pilot_version_conflict
8.1 ChannelStatus definitions (exact, testable)

Let days_elapsed = (today − launch_date).days, count = sales entries for the channel whose purchase date falls within [launch_date, launch_date + duration_days], and window_open = days_elapsed < duration_days. If launch_date is null, every channel is on_track with days_elapsed = 0 and null windows.

StatusCondition (evaluated in this precedence order)
passedcount >= success_threshold (target met, whether early or at window close)
killkill_threshold != null AND NOT window_open AND count < kill_threshold AND the experiment is NOT in kill_acknowledgments
killedSame as kill but the experiment IS in kill_acknowledgments (display overlay: red card + "Acknowledged on {date}" badge; if stopped_tracking, the channel is removed from the sales-entry dropdown)
failedNOT window_open AND count < success_threshold AND (kill_threshold == null OR count >= kill_threshold) — window closed between kill and success
warningwindow_open AND count < success_threshold AND days_elapsed >= ceil(duration_days * 0.5) — past the midpoint without meeting target
on_trackEverything else (window open, early or meeting pace)

The kill evaluation fires at window close because the B10 kill criteria are phrased as "<K sales in the first D days" — the verdict is only defined once D days have elapsed. Mid-window shortfalls surface as warning, not kill. The organic channel (E-005) has kill_threshold = null, so it can never enter kill/killed; its terminal states are passed or failed at day 56.

8.2 B10 thresholds, the 36-vs-40 gap, and channel attribution

The four upstream B10 experiment success thresholds sum to 36 (E-001: 15, E-002: 8, E-003: 8, E-004: 5). The pilot target is 40 distinct households. The remaining 4 are expected from organic word-of-mouth — referrals from the channel-driven families, shares by satisfied buyers in homeschool groups, and untracked direct outreach — consistent with the concept lock's founding-cohort hypothesis ("a loyal founding-family cohort that generates word-of-mouth before any arms-length marketing begins"). This spec adds E-005 Organic/Referral to close the gap explicitly.

ExperimentChannelKeySuccessKillBudgetDuration
E-001Communitycommunity≥15<5$3014d
E-002Partnershipspartnerships≥8<2$4521d
E-003Contentcontent≥8<2$3014d
E-004Paid Socialpaid_social≥5<2$8014d
E-005Organic/Referralorganic_referral≥4none$056d

Total success thresholds: 15 + 8 + 8 + 5 + 4 = 40, matching the pilot target. E-005 has no kill threshold because the operator cannot control or suppress word-of-mouth; its duration is the full 56-day pilot window.

Channel attribution methodology: sales channel attribution is operator judgment based on the purchaser's origin. The operator determines attribution by asking the buyer where they heard about the product (e.g., "Did you see this in a homeschool Facebook group, from a co-op organizer, or from a friend?") or by noting the context of the sale (e.g., a direct link shared in a specific group vs. an unprompted purchase). If the buyer cannot identify a specific tracked channel, the sale is attributed to organic/referral. The console provides no automated attribution mechanism. Misattribution affects threshold accuracy: assigning a community-channel sale to organic (or vice versa) inflates one channel's count and deflates another's, potentially masking a kill-threshold breach on the tracked channel or creating a false pass on organic. The operator should attribute conservatively — prefer the tracked channel when in doubt — and review the ledger periodically for accuracy. The Pilot screen displays a persistent note of this methodology above the sales entry form (§10.7).

Canonicality note: the upstream prose and JSON artifacts report slightly different budget figures for E-002/E-003/E-004. The thresholds live in a static config block inside the bridge (not read from upstream JSON at runtime, not persisted to pilot-state.json), are exposed via GET /api/pilot (§7.5a), and the implementer must reconcile this table against the B10 artifact at build time, treating the structured JSON values as canonical and documenting the reconciliation in a comment. The status math in §8.1 is independent of which budget figures are chosen.

9. Route Map and Navigation

BrowserRouter (hash-free). Persistent sidebar on desktop (fixed left, 240px), collapsible Sheet on mobile. Top header with app title and a global status strip showing last build outcome.

Accessibility requirements (binding):

  • Skip link: <a href="#main-content" class="sr-only focus:not-sr-only">Skip to main content</a> is the first focusable element in the DOM; visible on focus; activating it moves focus to the main content region.
  • Sidebar nav links carry aria-current="page" on the active route. Active state is signaled by icon-fill AND a left-border accent AND a text-weight change — never color alone.
  • Every iframe has a title attribute describing its content. Every icon-only button has an aria-label. Disabled buttons show a Tooltip explaining why.
  • Focus indicators: 2px ring, 2px offset, on all interactive elements, via :focus-visible; shadcn/ui defaults are retained, never overridden away.
  • Heading hierarchy: exactly one h1 per page (the screen name), h2 for sections, h3 for cards/subsections; no skipped levels.
RouteScreenPurpose
/DashboardPilot health, build/test status, quick actions, compliance alerts
/curriculumCurriculum LibraryBrowse all modules and bands in a two-pane layout
/curriculum/:moduleId/:bandKeyBand DetailRead-only lesson, tool, and checklist viewer for one band
/previewPack PreviewSelect module + band, view committed HTML or PDF in iframe
/buildBuild & ChecksTrigger full build, run tests, view logs, download artifacts
/launchLaunch ConfigEdit checkout URL and contact email; launch checklist; compliance posture
/pilotPilot TrackerTrack sales by channel, kill-threshold alerts with acknowledgment, feedback tally, acceptance checklist

Sidebar order (top to bottom): Dashboard, Curriculum, Preview, Build & Checks, Launch, Pilot. Each item has a lucide-react icon plus a text label.

10. Screen-by-Screen Specification

10.1 Dashboard (/)

Layout: Responsive grid — four metric cards on top row, two action cards below, alert banners above everything. Page heading: h1 "Dashboard".

Metric cards:

CardContentData Source
Pilot SalesDistinct purchasers / 40 target. Progress ring with ARIA value attributes. Red if any channel is in unacknowledged kill status.GET /api/pilot
FeedbackReports received / 20 target. Checklist-style display.GET /api/pilot
Time RemainingDays left in the 8-week window: max(0, 56 − days_since_launch). Countdown badge. "Set launch date" CTA if launch_date is null.GET /api/pilot
Build & TestLast build timestamp + success/failure badge. Last test pass/fail counts.GET /api/status

Action cards:

  • Quick Actions: Text-labeled primary buttons — "Build All" (POST /api/build), "Run Tests" (POST /api/test), "Preview Landing Page" (opens /site/index.html in a new tab), "Open Pilot Tracker" (navigates to /pilot). While an operation runs, the relevant buttons are disabled and show a Tooltip: "A build or test is currently running. Please wait for it to complete."
  • Recent Activity: Read-only scrolling panel of the last 10 bridge operations (builds, tests, config saves), timestamped. React state only, not persisted.

Alert banners (conditional, above cards):

  • config_error non-null: red Alert — "config.js could not be parsed: [error]. Fix the file or reset to defaults in Launch Config."
  • checkoutUrl blank: amber Alert — "Checkout URL is blank. Parents will see the honest 'opens at launch' message until a Gumroad or PayPal URL is saved in Launch Config."
  • Any pack stale: amber Alert — "Source has changed since last build. Stale packs: [slugs]. Click Build All to regenerate."
  • Any channel in kill (unacknowledged): red Alert — "[Channel] channel is below its kill threshold: [N] sales in the first [D] days; minimum is [K]. Go to Pilot Tracker to acknowledge."
  • Any channel killed (acknowledged): amber Alert — "[Channel] kill threshold acknowledged on [date]. Consider pivoting this channel."

Loading: All cards show Skeleton placeholders while GET /api/status and GET /api/pilot are in flight. If the bridge is unreachable, a persistent Alert appears at the top — "Console bridge not responding. Start it with python3 tools/console.py" — with a retry button. The alert appears only when the bridge is actually unreachable and disappears when it becomes reachable (verified by start/stop cycle). Bridge liveness is determined by a genuine GET /api/status request with a short timeout — no mocked transport, no fake health-check endpoint.

10.2 Curriculum Library (/curriculum)

Layout: Two-pane. Left sidebar (240px) module tree; right content area. Page heading: h1 "Curriculum Library".

Left pane — Module Tree:

  • Each module is a collapsible group showing title, domain badge, and lesson count.
  • Under each module, age bands as selectable rows: "Ages 5-8 (4 lessons, N tools)", "Ages 9-12 (4 lessons, N tools)"; Module 4 shows only "Ages 9-12 (4 lessons, 3 tools)".
  • Clicking a band navigates to /curriculum/:moduleId/:bandKey.
  • The tree uses role="tree" / role="treeitem", aria-expanded on collapsible groups, and visible focus rings.

Right pane (no selection): Product overview — name, subtitle, price, guarantee days, module count, total lessons (28 across 7 packs), compliance posture summary (COPPA: no child data; Module 4: concepts only; positioning: supplemental enrichment).

10.3 Band Detail (/curriculum/:moduleId/:bandKey)

Header: Module title (h2), age-band label, domain badge, back link to Curriculum Library. Parent intro text with "Show more / Show less" Collapsible. Module 4 shows a persistent badge: "Concepts only — no investment advice."

Tabs: Lessons | Tools | Checklist (TabsList with aria-label).

Lessons tab:

  • Accordion of lesson cards, one per week. Card header (h3): week number, title, minutes badge — red if >30 (a contract violation guardrail, not an amber caution, because the contract forbids exceeding 30 minutes).
  • Expanded card: materials list (pill/badge styled); full say script in a styled block; demonstrate steps as an ordered list; practice task and done_when criterion in a distinct panel with role="region" and aria-label="Practice task"; wrap_up if present.
  • Footer action: "Preview this pack" → /preview?module=:moduleId&band=:bandKey.

Tools tab:

  • A card per tool: kind icon (lucide-react), title (h3), metadata in a definition list (variant, rows, ingredients, steps…).
  • "Preview" button opens a Dialog containing <iframe title="Tool preview: {tool title}" src="/api/tools/{toolId}" />.

Checklist tab:

  • Table of checklist items with read-only checkboxes (visual only — the checklist is a printable artifact). Note below: "This checklist is part of the printable pack. It is displayed here for operator review."

Footer (all tabs): "Edit lesson content in content/curriculum.py using your text editor. After saving, click Build All to regenerate packs, then return here to see changes." with a "Copy path" button (aria-label="Copy file path to clipboard").

10.4 Pack Preview (/preview)

Selection bar: Select for module (4 options) and age band (2 options, or 1 for Module 4). URL query params (?module=…&band=…) pre-select on navigation from Band Detail. A third Select for an individual tool appears after a band is chosen, defaulting to "Full pack."

View toggle: Tabs with HTML | PDF | Source (aria-label="Preview format").

  • HTML tab: <iframe title="Pack preview: {module title} — {band label} (HTML)" src="/api/packs/{slug}/html" /> — the committed bytes, exactly what customers receive. The bridge reads committed files from disk on every request — no startup cache, no in-memory cache across requests. A text-labeled "Print" button calls iframe.contentWindow.print() (the pack's embedded @page { size: Letter; margin: 0.75in; } CSS handles page setup). A "Live render" Switch (aria-label="Live render from current source") swaps the iframe src to ?src=live to preview what current source would produce — useful after editing curriculum.py but before building. When a live-render subprocess fails, the bridge returns the HTML error page (§7.2a) and the iframe displays the styled error message in place — no raw JSON, no blank iframe. A text-labeled "Retry" button reloads the iframe after the operator fixes the source.
  • PDF tab: <iframe title="Pack preview: {module title} — {band label} (PDF)" src="/api/packs/{slug}/pdf" />; the browser's built-in viewer renders the US-Letter document. The bridge reads committed PDF files from disk on every request — no startup cache. "Download PDF" triggers a direct download. The live toggle points the iframe at ?src=live. On live-render error, the iframe displays the HTML error page (§7.2a) in place of the PDF — an iframe renders a text/html response regardless of what content type was expected, so no client-side fetch-and-inspect machinery is needed (§5.13).
  • Source tab: Read-only <pre> panel (role="region", aria-label="HTML source") showing the committed pack file's raw HTML.

Actions (all tabs): "Download HTML", "Download PDF", "Open in new tab" — text+icon buttons, each with an aria-label.

Loading: Iframes show a Skeleton until loaded; during live renders the container shows a spinner with aria-busy="true" and an aria-live="polite" announcement "Loading preview…".

Compliance note: if checkoutUrl is blank, a subtle notice below the preview: "The buy button on this pack's landing page will display 'opens at launch' until a checkout URL is configured."

10.5 Build & Checks (/build)

Action bar: two buttons (partial builds removed), disabled while any operation is active; disabled buttons show a Tooltip — "A build or test is currently running. Please wait for it to complete."

  • "Full build (HTML + PDF + zips)" → POST /api/build
  • "Run test suite" → POST /api/test

While running: the button shows a spinner with elapsed timer ("Running… 3.2s") and aria-busy="true"; an aria-live="polite" region announces "Build in progress" / "Build complete".

Output panel: Scrollable ScrollArea with monospace pre styling showing captured stdout/stderr. Output appends across sequential actions; a text-labeled "Clear log" button resets it.

Results summary (post-build):

  • On success (BuildResult.ok === true): Table of artifacts: Slug | HTML ✓/✗ | PDF ✓/✗ | HTML size | PDF size | Status (Fresh/Stale/Missing badge, icon+text) | Actions (Preview, Download HTML, Download PDF — all aria-labeled). Table of zip bundles: Name | Size | Exists? | Actions (Download from /artifacts/{name}, Copy path). Toast: "Build complete: 7 HTML, 7 PDF, 5 zips generated in [duration]".
  • On build failure (BuildResult.ok === false): red Alert with error excerpt; full stderr in the log; best-effort partial artifact and zip tables showing whatever files exist on disk (from BuildResult.artifacts and BuildResult.zips, §5.14). Toast: "Build failed: [error excerpt]".
  • On timeout (standard error envelope): red Alert — "Build timed out after 120 seconds. The process was terminated. Try again or run python3 tools/build.py in a terminal."

Results summary (post-test):

  • Summary bar: "48 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors in [duration]" (green) or "N passed, N failed, M errors" (red).
  • On failures: red Alert with count, then an Accordion of failing tests (h3 headers); each expands to the captured traceback in a monospace panel.
  • "Copy raw output" button (aria-label="Copy test output to clipboard").
  • On timeout: red Alert — "Test suite timed out after 120 seconds. The process was terminated. A test may be hanging."

Contract validation badges (derived from test results, never duplicated logic): the console maps test class names from the most recent test run to contract labels:

const CONTRACT_BADGES = [
  { test_class: "TestModuleShape",        label: "4 modules with correct age bands" },
  { test_class: "TestLessonContract",     label: "All lessons ≤30 minutes with required fields" },
  { test_class: "TestModule4Compliance",  label: "Module 4: no banned investment language" },
  { test_class: "TestToolsAndChecklists", label: "All bands have required tool kinds" },
];

The implementer verifies the actual class names from tests/ source. Each badge shows green (all tests in the class passed), red with the failing test name, or gray "Not run" before any test execution. If a mapped class name is absent from the results — e.g., the suite renamed it — the badge shows gray "Not checked," never a false green. The test suite remains the single source of truth; drift surfaces visibly instead of silently.

Staleness alert: if any pack's committed files are older than the maximum mtime of the §6.7 source files, an amber banner tops the screen: "Source has changed since last build. Stale packs: [slugs]. Click Full build to regenerate."

10.6 Launch Config (/launch)

Config form:

  • Input + Label "Gumroad or PayPal product URL." Validation: https://… or empty; must not contain </script. Inline error and disabled Save on invalid input.
  • Input + Label "Customer contact email." Validation: ^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$ or empty. If the value is pilot@example.com, an amber note: "This is the default placeholder. Update it before launch."
  • Overwrite warning (persistent, visible before the operator ever clicks Save): an info Alert — "Saving via this form replaces the entire site/assets/config.js file. Any custom comments, fields, or formatting added by hand will be overwritten. To preserve manual edits, edit the file directly instead."
  • "Save" → PUT /api/config; success toast: "Launch config saved. Buy buttons will now link to your checkout." Field errors render inline on failure.
  • "Test checkout link" opens the configured URL in a new tab (disabled if blank; aria-label="Open checkout URL in new tab").

Corruption state: if GET /api/config reports config_corrupted, the form fields are disabled, a red Alert shows the parse error, and a "Reset to defaults" button regenerates a valid file (§7.4).

Launch checklist: interactive checkboxes persisted to localStorage under lsf_launch_checklist (UI convenience, not pilot data):

  1. Set checkout link in config ← auto-checked when checkoutUrl is non-blank
  2. Host landing page on static host
  3. Upload zip bundles to file host
  4. Verify buy button reaches checkout
  5. Enable 2FA on Gumroad/PayPal account
  6. Verify pack PDFs print correctly on home printer

Compliance posture (static cards, h2 "Compliance Posture"):

  • "No child accounts or data collected (COPPA)" — the console never adds inputs a child might fill in.
  • "Module 4: concepts only, no investment advice" — tests enforce banned-term lists.
  • "Supplemental enrichment, not accredited curriculum."
  • "7-day money-back guarantee" — from product constants.

File paths reference: read-only list with "Copy path" buttons (each aria-label="Copy {description} path"): content/curriculum.py ("Edit lesson content here"), site/assets/config.js ("Checkout configuration — edited above; hand-edits will be overwritten"), packaging.json, dist/ ("Customer zip bundles, generated by Build All"), OPERATOR_GUIDE.md.

Operator guide: ScrollArea (aria-label="Operator guide") rendering OPERATOR_GUIDE.md via a lightweight markdown renderer (e.g., marked). Read-only.

10.7 Pilot Tracker (/pilot)

Setup row:

  • Launch date picker (Input type="date" + Label). Changing it updates the countdown and recomputes all threshold windows.
  • "Days remaining": max(0, 56 − days_since_launch); if launch_date is null, "Pilot not started."

Channel attribution note (persistent, above the sales entry form): a small info Alert — "Channel attribution is your judgment. Ask the buyer where they heard about the product. Misattribution affects threshold accuracy — when in doubt, prefer the tracked channel." This surfaces the §8.2 attribution methodology directly in the operator's workflow.

Sales entry form:

  • Input + Label "Purchaser email" (required).
  • Select for channel: Community (E-001), Partnerships (E-002), Content (E-003), Paid Social (E-004), Organic/Referral (E-005). Channels with stopped_tracking: true are removed from this dropdown.
  • Input type="date" + Label "Purchase date" (default today).
  • "Add sale" appends to the ledger and persists via PUT /api/pilot (sending the current _version for optimistic concurrency; on 409, the VersionConflictDialog opens — §5.5, §7.5).
  • Duplicate detection: emails are normalized by trim() + case-folding before comparison — existing.email.trim().toLowerCase() === newEmail.trim().toLowerCase(). This normalization is performed server-side by the bridge (§7.5) so that direct API calls also enforce it. A duplicate shows an inline warning: "This email is already in the ledger (entered on {date}). Add anyway?" with a confirm button. Confirmed duplicates count toward total sales but not toward distinct purchasers.

Version conflict handling: when PUT /api/pilot returns HTTP 409 with type: "pilot_version_conflict", the VersionConflictDialog opens: "This pilot data was updated in another tab. The latest version has been loaded, including [N] sales entries. Please review your changes and re-enter them." The dialog reads the current sales count from the response's data field and offers two buttons: "Reload and re-enter" (invalidates ['pilot'] to refetch, closes the dialog, restores the form with the operator's unsaved entry pre-filled for re-submission) and "Discard my entry" (refetches and clears the form).

Email masking (in the ledger):

  • Split at @ into local and domain.
  • If local.length >= 3: show first 2 characters + + @ + full domain (jane.doe@gmail.com → ja@gmail.com).
  • If local.length < 3: show + @ + full domain (a@b.co → @b.co).
  • The full email never appears in the table; clicking a row reveals it in an operator-only detail panel.

Sales ledger: Table — Email (masked) | Channel | Date | Actions (Delete, aria-label="Delete sale entry for {masked email}"). Sortable by date and channel; filterable by channel via a Select (aria-label="Filter by channel"). Delete requires a confirmation Dialog — it corrects operator-entered data; it is not a product-file operation.

Metrics cards:

  • Distinct purchasers (unique normalized emails) / 40 — Progress bar with aria-valuenow/-min/-max.
  • Feedback reports / 20 — Progress bar plus a text-labeled "+1 report" button.
  • Total sales entries (including duplicates) — informational only.

Kill-threshold tracker: five ChannelCards (E-001…E-005), each showing: experiment ID and channel name (h3); current in-window count; success threshold (green badge, check icon): "Target: N sales"; kill threshold (red badge, alert icon): "Kill if < K sales in first D days" — E-005 shows "No kill threshold — passive channel"; budget; window ("{start} to {end}" or "not started"); days elapsed/remaining; and a status indicator with icon+text per §8.1: green "On track", amber "Warning: N sales, D days left", red "Kill triggered", dark-red "Killed — acknowledged {date}", blue "Passed: target met", gray "Failed: window closed below target". All threshold values are read from the thresholds array in the GET /api/pilot response (§7.5a) — never hardcoded in the client.

Kill-threshold acknowledgment (binding experiment guard):

  1. When a channel's status becomes kill, its card turns red and a KillAcknowledgmentDialog opens automatically on the Pilot screen: "Kill threshold breached: {channel}. {N} sales in the first {D} days; minimum is {K}. This channel is not performing. Acknowledge to continue tracking, or acknowledge and stop entering sales for this channel."
  2. Two buttons: "Acknowledge and continue" (records kill_acknowledgments[experiment_id] = { acknowledged_at: today, stopped_tracking: false }) and "Acknowledge and stop this channel" (same, with stopped_tracking: true, removing the channel from the sales-entry dropdown).
  3. Until acknowledged, a persistent red banner appears on the Dashboard and Pilot screens: "Unacknowledged kill threshold: [Channel]. Go to Pilot Tracker to acknowledge."
  4. After acknowledgment the banner clears; the card shows killed with "Acknowledged on {date}". If tracking continues, each subsequent sale entered for that channel shows a brief reminder: "This channel's kill threshold was acknowledged on {date}."

The console never locks the operator out of their own data; it creates a deliberate, recorded checkpoint so a breached walk-away gate cannot pass silently. The operator decides; the console insists the decision be conscious.

Acceptance checklist: four checkboxes persisted to pilot state via PUT /api/pilot:

  1. 40+ distinct purchaser households (unique emails, case-insensitive)
  2. Buyer purchases and receives files without per-transaction operator intervention
  3. 20+ families submitted usable completion reports
  4. Reports confirm ≤30 min lessons, no advance planning, and genuine skill tasks per B6 definitions

Export and reset:

  • "Export pilot data" (aria-label="Export pilot data as JSON") downloads pilot-state.json (without the injected thresholds — the export is the raw persisted state, matching the file on disk).
  • "Reset pilot data" (destructive variant) opens a Dialog requiring the operator to type RESET: "This will permanently delete all sales records, feedback counts, acceptance checklist state, and kill acknowledgments. Build/test history is NOT affected. This cannot be undone." On confirm, the console calls POST /api/pilot/reset (§7.3), which writes the §6.4 default object with _version: 0 directly, bypassing the optimistic-concurrency guard. The VersionConflictDialog never appears during reset — the dedicated endpoint performs no version check. console/data/console-state.json is untouched, and no product file is involved. The button is labeled "Reset pilot data" — not "Reset all" — to describe exactly what is cleared. The dedicated POST /api/pilot/reset endpoint exists because a PUT /api/pilot with _version: 0 would always be rejected as a version conflict when the stored version is greater than zero.

12. State Management and Data Fetching

Server state — TanStack Query
['status']           // GET /api/status
['curriculum']       // GET /api/curriculum
['packs']            // GET /api/packs
['config']           // GET /api/config
['pilot']            // GET /api/pilot  — includes _version and thresholds (injected by bridge)
['packaging']        // GET /api/packaging

Configuration: staleTime 5 minutes for curriculum and packaging; 0 for status, packs, config, pilot. refetchOnWindowFocus: true for status and pilot. retry: 1 (bridge failures are usually "not running," not transient).

Mutations:

['buildAll']    // POST /api/build → invalidate ['packs'], ['status'], ['curriculum']
['runTests']    // POST /api/test  → invalidate ['status']
['saveConfig']  // PUT /api/config → invalidate ['config'], ['status']
['savePilot']   // PUT /api/pilot  → invalidate ['pilot'], ['status']
['resetPilot']  // POST /api/pilot/reset → invalidate ['pilot'], ['status']

buildAll invalidates ['curriculum'] deliberately: a successful build follows a source edit, so the Curriculum screen refetches (from a fresh subprocess import) and shows updated content without a bridge restart. Every mutation disables its trigger button while pending, shows an explanatory Tooltip on the disabled button, and toasts on success or error.

Pilot save with concurrency control: savePilot reads the current _version from the cached ['pilot'] data and includes it in the PUT body. The thresholds field in the PilotState type is a client-side read-only artifact of the GET response; the client does not send it in the PUT body (or if it does, the bridge strips it server-side per §7.5 — the bridge stripping is the binding requirement). On HTTP 409 (pilot_version_conflict), the mutation's onError handler opens the VersionConflictDialog populated from the response body's data field (the current stored state, carried by the 409 so no extra round-trip is needed to display it), invalidates ['pilot'] to sync the cache to the fresh _version, and lets the operator re-enter their changes.

Pilot reset: resetPilot calls POST /api/pilot/reset — a dedicated endpoint that writes the default object with _version: 0 without checking the stored version (§7.3). This bypasses the optimistic-concurrency guard by design, because the stored version will almost always be greater than 0, making a PUT-based reset impossible. The typed-RESET confirmation in the UI is the safeguard; the endpoint itself is unguarded by version but gated by the UI. On success, ['pilot'] and ['status'] are invalidated.

Build failure handling: because build failures arrive as { ok: true, data: BuildResult } with BuildResult.ok === false (§5.14), buildAll does not throw on build failure; callers inspect result.ok and render the partial artifact table from result.artifacts/result.zips alongside the error alert. Timeout, lock contention, and source errors arrive as standard error envelopes and throw.

Client state — React useState + localStorage

No global state library. Client-only state: selectedModuleId/selectedBandKey and activeTab (useState in route components); buildLog (useState, not persisted); pilotFormValues (useState, committed on submit); launchChecklist and sidebar-collapsed (localStorage, UI convenience only). Pilot data is never in localStorage — it round-trips through console/data/pilot-state.json via the bridge.

API client module (console/src/lib/api.ts)
const BASE = ''; // same-origin in production; proxied in dev

const TIMEOUTS = { build: 130_000, test: 130_000, preview: 35_000, default: 30_000 };

export class BridgeError extends Error {
  type?: string;
  data?: unknown;
  constructor(message: string, type?: string, data?: unknown) {
    super(message);
    this.name = 'BridgeError';
    this.type = type;
    this.data = data;
  }
}

async function rpc<T>(path: string, options?: RequestInit & { timeout?: number }): Promise<T> {
  const timeout = options?.timeout ?? TIMEOUTS.default;
  const controller = new AbortController();
  const timer = setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), timeout);
  try {
    const res = await fetch(`${BASE}${path}`, {
      ...options,
      signal: controller.signal,
      headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', ...options?.headers },
    });
    if (res.status === 409) {
      // Distinguish pilot version conflict from build-lock contention by body type
      const body = await res.json();
      throw new BridgeError(
        body.error || 'Conflict',
        body.type,                       // 'pilot_version_conflict' | 'lock_contention'
        body.data,                       // current pilot state, for version conflicts
      );
    }
    const json: BridgeResponse<T> = await res.json();
    if (!json.ok) throw new BridgeError(json.error, json.type);
    return json.data;
  } finally {
    clearTimeout(timer);
  }
}

export const api = {
  getStatus:    () => rpc<StatusResponse>('/api/status'),
  getCurriculum:() => rpc<CurriculumData>('/api/curriculum'),
  getPackList:  () => rpc<PackSummary[]>('/api/packs'),
  getPackHtmlUrl:(slug: string, live = false) => `${BASE}/api/packs/${slug}/html${live ? '?src=live' : ''}`,
  getPackPdfUrl: (slug: string, live = false) => `${BASE}/api/packs/${slug}/pdf${live ? '?src=live' : ''}`,
  getToolHtmlUrl:(toolId: string) => `${BASE}/api/tools/${toolId}`,
  buildAll:     () => rpc<BuildResult>('/api/build', { method: 'POST', timeout: TIMEOUTS.build }),
  runTests:     () => rpc<TestResult>('/api/test',  { method: 'POST', timeout: TIMEOUTS.test }),
  getConfig:    () => rpc<ConfigState>('/api/config'),
  saveConfig:   (body: { checkoutUrl: string; contactEmail: string }) =>
                  rpc<ConfigState>('/api/config', { method: 'PUT', body: JSON.stringify(body) }),
  getPilot:     () => rpc<PilotState>('/api/pilot'),
  savePilot:    (body: PilotState) =>
                  rpc<PilotState>('/api/pilot', { method: 'PUT', body: JSON.stringify(body) }),
  resetPilot:   () => rpc<PilotState>('/api/pilot/reset', { method: 'POST' }),
};

Callers discriminate errors via err.type: pilot_version_conflict (open VersionConflictDialog with err.data), lock_contention (toast: "A build or test is already running…"), source_error, timeout, config_corrupted, pilot_corrupted (screen-level red Alerts per §13).

14. Compliance Guardrails Surfaced in the UI

COPPA — No child data

The console never renders an input that a child might fill in. The sales ledger collects purchaser (parent) emails only; emails are masked in the table. No child name, age, or personal data field exists anywhere. The Launch compliance card states: "No child accounts or data collected. The product and this console are COPPA-compliant by design."

Module 4 — Concepts only

Band Detail for Module 4 carries the persistent badge "Concepts only — no investment advice." The Build screen's TestModule4Compliance badge reflects the test suite's actual result — the console never re-implements banned-term logic. If the last test run flagged Module 4, the Curriculum Library shows an orange badge next to it.

Honest checkout

If checkoutUrl is blank, the Dashboard, Launch, and Preview surfaces say so, and Preview notes the buy button will display "opens at launch." The console never fakes a URL and never bypasses site.js's validation: PUT /api/config enforces the same https-or-empty rule, with injection-safe escaping (§7.4).

No custom platform

No storefront, accounts, customer forms, or recurring billing are built. The Launch compliance cards and §15 reinforce this posture.

15. Explicit Non-Goals

  • No content editing in the browser. Lesson text is edited in content/curriculum.py in the operator's editor. The console is read-only for all content.
  • No replacement of the customer-facing site/ with React. Landing and pack pages remain static, Python-generated, and test-validated. The console previews them; it never re-renders them.
  • No real-time sales API integration. Sales are manually entered. Gumroad/PayPal API integration is deferred to a future spec if the pilot succeeds.
  • No collaborative editing or multi-user support. One operator, one browser, one machine.
  • No mobile-optimized operator UI. Desktop-first; the layout stacks on narrow screens but is not designed for phone use.
  • No PDF editing or generation in the browser. PDFs come from the Python renderers only; the browser displays and downloads them.
  • No authentication or authorization. Loopback binding + exact-match Host guard + Origin allowlist; no CORS headers; no login screen.
  • No build-time Node scripts that modify Python source files. The Vite build emits static assets only; the bridge never writes Python source.
  • No child-facing features. No child accounts, forms, or data collection.
  • No destructive actions against product files. The only product-file mutation is site/assets/config.js via validated PUT /api/config. Pilot reset clears console/data/pilot-state.json only (via POST /api/pilot/reset); console/data/console-state.json and all product files are untouched.
  • No modification to the build pipeline. tools/build.py is unchanged. No build manifest is written anywhere. Freshness is mtime comparison only.
  • No importlib.reload. All product-module access happens in fresh subprocesses. No hot-reloading of any kind.
  • No partial build endpoints. Only POST /api/build (full) and POST /api/test are exposed.
  • No platform-specific signal handling. Subprocess termination uses Popen.terminate() and Popen.kill() only — never os.kill with signal.SIGTERM or signal.SIGKILL.
  • No hardcoded 'python3' subprocess executable. All subprocess calls use sys.executable to satisfy the cross-platform commitment.
  • No dev-mode widening of the Host allowlist. The Host guard accepts exactly two values in every mode; only the Origin allowlist widens under --dev, and only by the Vite dev origin.
  • No startup-time caching of committed pack files. Pack HTML and PDF endpoints read from disk on every request. No in-memory cache of file bytes exists in the bridge.
  • No persistence of thresholds to pilot-state.json. The bridge strips thresholds from PUT bodies and always injects from its static config on GET.

16. Debt Carried Forward and Bounded Choices

ItemStatusTreatment
B9 lists $9.97/mo subscription; B6/Selected Problem locks $25 one-time pilot priceUnresolved upstream debtConsole displays PRICE_USD from content/curriculum.py (currently 25). Pilot tracker targets 40 one-time sales, not subscription metrics. If upstream reconciles, the console reads the new price from source — no code change.
B7 WTP hypothesis is $10/mo; product is $25 one-timeUnresolved upstream debtThe console does not display WTP. The pilot tracker records actual sales count and channel attribution — the falsifiable metrics.
B10 thresholds are hypotheses, not verified requirementsEpistemic status: hypothesisThreshold cards are labeled "Experiment threshold," not "Requirement." Thresholds live in a static config block in the bridge and are exposed via GET /api/pilot (§7.5a); they are never persisted to pilot-state.json — the bridge strips them from PUT bodies and always injects from its static config on GET (§7.5a). A future spec can make them operator-editable if pilot data warrants.
B10 success thresholds sum to 36; pilot target is 40Resolved in this specE-005 Organic/Referral (≥4, no kill, 56d) closes the gap to 40, consistent with the concept lock's word-of-mouth hypothesis.
E-005 channel attribution methodologyBounded assumptionAttribution is operator judgment based on asking the buyer (§8.2). Misattribution affects threshold math; conservative attribution (prefer the tracked channel) is recommended. Surfaced as a persistent note in the Pilot Tracker UI (§10.7). No automated attribution mechanism is built.
console/data/pilot-state.json, console/data/console-state.json (gitignored)Bounded local stateOperator-machine-only; never deployed; absent-safe with §6.4 defaults; both written atomically (temp file + os.replace) so no reader can observe a partial write; console/data/ directory created by bridge via os.makedirs(..., exist_ok=True) before every write path (not just build/test); export-to-JSON provides portability.
Concurrent pilot-state saves risk lost updatesBounded safetyOptimistic concurrency via bridge-managed _version integer (§5.5, §7.5); mismatch returns HTTP 409 carrying the current state; the VersionConflictDialog drives reload-and-re-enter. Integer comparison is exact — no timestamp-granularity edge cases. Pilot reset uses a dedicated POST /api/pilot/reset endpoint that bypasses the version check, because a PUT with _version: 0 would always be rejected when the stored version is >0.
Config write is the only product-file mutationBounded, reversibleValidated, template-generated, injection-escaped; persistent overwrite warning; the operator may always hand-edit instead. Template uses double-quoted JSON keys so the bridge's own parser round-trips the file (§7.4). Parser uses json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode() to handle braces inside string values (§7.4).
Backend function signatures and constants unverified at spec timeVerification step mandated§7.1 tables for both function signatures and module-level constants; implementer verifies against source, adapts the wrapper internally, documents divergences; endpoint contracts do not change. render_pack_pdf's return type is handled defensively (§6.3) until verified.
B10 budget figures differ between upstream prose and JSONBounded assumptionStatic bridge config uses the structured-artifact values (§8.2); the reconciliation is documented in a code comment. Status math is independent of the figures.
All subprocess calls have server-side timeoutsBounded safety120s build/test, 30s others; kill sequence Popen.terminate() → 5s wait → Popen.kill() → final communicate() to reap; cross-platform (no os.kill, no signal constants); executable is sys.executable (not 'python3'); lock released in finally; client timeouts are deliberately longer so structured errors arrive first.
Freshness detection covers all source filesBounded correctness§6.7: max mtime across content/curriculum.py, tools/render_html.py, tools/render_pdf.py, tools/pdfgen.py, tools/build.py. Any source edit triggers staleness; false positives prompt a safe idempotent rebuild; the list must be updated if the pipeline gains files.
Wrapper sys.path must include repo rootMandatory implementation detail§6.3 specifies sys.path.insert(0, os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))) at the top of tools/console_bridge.py before any product import, using __file__-based resolution. Without it, ModuleNotFoundError is misattributed as a curriculum source error.
Pilot threshold metadata must be exposed to client and never persistedBounded safety§7.5a: GET /api/pilot response includes thresholds array injected from the bridge's static config; PUT /api/pilot strips thresholds from the request body before writing to disk; the file never contains thresholds. Client renders ChannelCard from this data, never from hardcoded constants. Prevents client/bridge drift if B10 reconciliation changes values.
Pilot reset must bypass optimistic concurrencyMandatory implementation detail§7.3: dedicated POST /api/pilot/reset endpoint writes the default object with _version: 0 without checking the stored version. A PUT /api/pilot with _version: 0 would always be rejected when stored version >0, making a PUT-based reset action dead code. The typed-RESET confirmation in the UI is the safeguard.
Live-render error page must HTML-escape error textMandatory implementation detail§7.2a: the bridge calls html.escape(error_text, quote=True) on the stderr excerpt before inserting it into the HTML error page template. This prevents error text containing <script> or other HTML markup from executing in the iframe context. Applies to all failure types on all three live-render routes; AC-43 verifies with an injected <script> payload.
PDF temp file must survive wrapper exitMandatory implementation detail§6.3: wrapper uses tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False); bridge reads bytes, serves them, then os.unlink() in finally. Default delete=True would remove the file when the wrapper exits, causing FileNotFoundError on every PDF live-render.
Test wrapper must capture all stdoutMandatory implementation detail§7.7: contextlib.redirect_stdout into StringIO wraps the entire test execution, not just the TextTestRunner stream. Without this, print() in test code or imported modules corrupts the JSON envelope.
Config parser must handle braces in stringsMandatory implementation detail§7.4: json.JSONDecoder().raw_decode() replaces naive find('}'). Handles } inside URL query parameters and other string values. Also searches for = before { to skip comment braces.
Console/data directory creation must precede every write pathMandatory implementation detail§6.2: os.makedirs('console/data', exist_ok=True) is called before every write to either state file — not just build/test writes. A pilot save as the first operation on a fresh clone must also succeed.
Validator finding countFactual correction§7 correctly states 117 endpoint_missing findings (matching the validator's actual output), not 105. The argument — routes are new, not pre-existing — is unaffected by the count.

  2. Open browser to http://127.0.0.1:8787

  4. If launching: Launch screen → paste Gumroad/PayPal URL → Save → "Test checkout link"
  5. As sales come in: Pilot screen → enter email, channel, date → track progress against thresholds
