18. Acceptance Criteria

Each criterion is written to resist degenerate solutions — a token implementation that satisfies the letter while violating the intent must fail. Where a criterion could be gamed by hardcoding responses to specific test inputs, the criterion requires verification against held-out or independently generated values. Each criterion specifies multiple test cases to prevent single-case hardcoding.

  1. Console starts and serves a fully data-driven SPA. After python3 tools/console.py, http://127.0.0.1:8787 renders the SPA with a persistent sidebar linking to all six screens; each route loads its specified layout and makes at least one successful API call that returns data derived from the current filesystem state (fresh subprocess reads), not pre-serialized snapshots. Verify by touching at least two source files from different categories (e.g., content/curriculum.py and tools/render_html.py) independently and observing the SPA reflect the changed freshness state without a bridge restart after each touch. Additionally, touch a file NOT in the SOURCE_FILES list (e.g., README.md) and confirm the stale warning does NOT appear — proving the freshness check uses the defined source set, not a broader heuristic. If console/dist/ is missing, the bridge prints setup instructions and exits non-zero. If tools/console_bridge.py is missing, the bridge prints a wrapper-missing error and exits non-zero. No screen may consist solely of hardcoded placeholders.
  1. Curriculum data is served by a fresh Python subprocess that imports the product module on every call. Modify a lesson title in content/curriculum.py without running any build or other action. Immediately request GET /api/curriculum; the response must contain the updated title, proving the API call itself reads the source file fresh — not from a cache invalidated by a build trigger. Use a randomly generated string (e.g., a UUID) as the new title to prevent pre-baked responses from matching. Additionally verify that a new Python process spawns per curriculum API call by monitoring the process tree (e.g., ps on Unix, tasklist on Windows) during the request — no imported module state persists across calls. The screen shows 4 modules with correct bands (Modules 1–3: two bands; Module 4: 9-12 only) and 28 lessons. No importlib.reload, no persistent caches, no in-process module imports in the bridge, no on-disk caching of prior subprocess output.
  1. Band Detail is derived from a live API call that reads the source file for every lesson. An automated test enumerates all modules, bands, and lessons; for each lesson, compares every field (title, minutes, materials, say, demonstrate, practice, done_when, wrap_up) against the contents of content/curriculum.py parsed by an independent Python script. Any mismatch for any lesson indicates a failure — no lesson may be served from a static payload. Additionally, edit a displayed lesson field in content/curriculum.py with an unpredictable value (e.g., a random UUID inserted into a say line) and confirm the Band Detail view shows that exact value after navigation (no rebuild or restart required), proving the data comes from a live API call, not a hardcoded payload.
  1. Pack Preview HTML is byte-identical to committed files and read fresh from disk on every request. For every slug, GET /api/packs/<slug>/html returns bytes identical to site/packs/<slug>.html; verify by scripting a diff across all seven slugs. Additionally, after a successful build that regenerates the packs, request the HTML endpoint and confirm the response bytes match the newly written file, not the pre-build state — this rules out a startup-time cache. Manually overwrite a committed HTML file with known different content and verify the endpoint returns the new content without a bridge restart. The iframe has a title; the Print button opens the browser print dialog.
  1. Pack Preview PDF is byte-identical to committed files and read fresh from disk on every request. For every slug, GET /api/packs/<slug>/pdf returns the exact bytes of site/packs/pdf/<slug>.pdf; checksum comparison across all seven passes; downloads begin with %PDF-1.4. Additionally, after a full build that regenerates the PDFs, immediately request the PDF endpoint and compare byte-for-byte with the newly created file. Manually replace the on-disk PDF with a known different file and confirm the endpoint returns the new bytes without a bridge restart. The iframe has a title.
  1. HTML live render is the output of the actual render_pack_html subprocess. Insert a randomly generated, unpredictable string (e.g., a UUID) into a say line in content/curriculum.py after the bridge is running; ?src=live shows the random string without a build; the committed view does not contain it. Verify by diffing the live response against the output of an independent manual run (python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0, '.'); from content.curriculum import *; from tools.render_html import render_pack_html; ...") that calls render_pack_html with the same source. The two outputs must match; text substitution or patching of committed files must be detectable as a mismatch. Monitor process creation to confirm a fresh subprocess spawns for each live-render request — ruling out pre-generated or cached responses. Live render completes within 30 seconds or returns a structured timeout.
  1. PDF live render is the output of the actual render_pack_pdf subprocess. After inserting an unpredictable curriculum edit (random token in a say block) with the bridge running, ?src=live on the PDF endpoint returns a valid PDF reflecting the edit; the committed PDF is unchanged. Verify by comparing the live PDF to an independently generated PDF using the same source edit (via a separate subprocess call with the verified return-type handling, §6.3); a byte-level comparison must match, allowing for non-deterministic metadata such as creation timestamps. Confirm a fresh subprocess is created for each request via OS process monitoring. The wrapper's return-type chain is verified against source and simplified to the true call chain, with a comment. The response begins with %PDF-1.4. Verify that the temp file survives the wrapper's exit by confirming the bridge reads and serves it (no FileNotFoundError); the wrapper must use delete=False.
  1. Full build executes the real pipeline and regenerates files on disk. After "Full build," every artifact in the table exists with mtimes newer than before the build, and table sizes match os.stat sizes. Verify that the captured log output contains expected messages from tools/build.py (rendering messages, zip creation messages — not a fabricated log), and that artifact files are byte-identical to those produced by a manual python3 tools/build.py run on the same source code. A simple mtime check is insufficient. The build completes within 120 seconds or returns a structured timeout. POST /api/build/html and POST /api/build/pdf return 404.
  1. Test run executes the real suite. Break a test deliberately; the console reports the failure with test name and traceback. Restore it; the suite returns to 48 passed / 0 failed. Results come from the wrapper's programmatic unittest JSON (§7.7), not regex over human output, within 120 seconds or a structured timeout. Verify that no stray print output corrupts the JSON envelope — the wrapper must capture all stdout via redirect_stdout (§7.7). Insert a print("DEBUG") into a test and confirm it appears in the stdout field of the JSON response, not mixed into the JSON envelope.
  1. Launch Config persists, validates, and round-trips for multiple input sets. Save at least two different sets of valid configuration values (e.g., https://gumroad.com/l/product-a + operator@example.com, then https://paypal.me/another + parent.contact@host.org): the on-disk site/assets/config.js contains the values with json.dumps + \u003c/\u003e escaping and double-quoted keys ("checkoutUrl", "contactEmail") in both cases; after a bridge restart GET /api/config returns each saved set without config_corrupted. Non-https URLs, values containing </script, and malformed emails are rejected and leave the file untouched. The overwrite warning is visible before the first save. Round-trip check: the file written by PUT /api/config must be parseable by the bridge's own GET /api/config parser without errors for both input sets. Brace-in-value check: save a URL containing } (e.g., https://example.com/callback?data={token}); GET /api/config must return the saved value without config_corrupted, proving the raw_decode parser handles braces inside JSON strings.
  1. Config corruption recovers from multiple malformation patterns. Write at least three different types of corrupt content into site/assets/config.js: (a) invalid JSON like { corrupt, (b) a truncated window.LSF_CONFIG = { with no closing brace, (c) a valid JSON object missing the window.LSF_CONFIG marker. For each, GET /api/config returns type: "config_corrupted"; Dashboard and Launch show the red alert; "Reset to defaults" regenerates a valid file. Verify by reading the file afterward and confirming GET /api/config succeeds on it for each corruption case. The corruption detection must rely on a genuine parse attempt using raw_decode, not string matching against specific malformations.
  1. Pilot Tracker persists, normalizes on the server for varied emails, and survives restarts. Send multiple held-out email strings with varying whitespace, case, and domain formatting via direct API calls (curl): " Jane@Example.COM ", "user@domain.com", " USER@DOMAIN.COM", "User@Domain.com". After each PUT, the GET response must show the normalized version ("jane@example.com", "user@domain.com") — server-side normalization, not client-side. Send a subsequent sale with "jane@example.com" after " Jane@Example.COM "; the bridge must detect a duplicate (distinct-purchaser count unchanged). A sale appears in console/data/pilot-state.json and survives a bridge restart. The stored file must contain the normalized data, not the original. All normalization and duplicate detection verified by raw API calls that bypass the UI.
  1. Threshold math and acknowledgment flow are exact across a matrix of states. Enumerate at least five distinct pilot state configurations covering all six status branches (on_track, warning, kill, killed, passed, failed). For each configuration (combination of launch date, per-channel sales counts, and elapsed days), the computed ChannelStatus must match the rules in §8.1 exactly. Configurations must include: (a) early window with sales meeting pace → on_track; (b) past midpoint below target → warning; (c) window closed below kill threshold, unacknowledged → kill; (d) window closed below kill threshold, acknowledged → killed; (e) window closed above success threshold → passed; (f) window closed between kill and success → failed. The acknowledgment dialog auto-opens for kill, records kill_acknowledgments on confirm, clears the banner, and shows "Acknowledged on {date}." "Stop this channel" removes the channel from the entry dropdown. Threshold values displayed in ChannelCards must match the thresholds array from GET /api/pilot — not hardcoded constants. Modify the bridge's static threshold block and confirm the client displays the updated values after a refetch — no client code change required.
  1. Stale-pack warning triggers and clears for every source file. Programmatically touch each file in the SOURCE_FILES list individually (content/curriculum.py, tools/render_html.py, tools/render_pdf.py, tools/pdfgen.py, tools/build.py — one at a time, restoring mtimes between tests): after each touch, the warning appears on Dashboard and Build with affected slugs. Run a full build: it disappears. Additionally, touch a file NOT in the SOURCE_FILES list (e.g., README.md) and verify the warning does NOT appear — proving the list is exhaustive and correctly implemented.
  1. Checkout warning toggles for multiple URL values. Test with at least three distinct valid HTTPS URLs (e.g., https://gumroad.com/l/abc, https://paypal.me/test, https://example.com/buy): saving each clears the amber warning. Test with at least three distinct empty/invalid states (empty string, http:// prefix, whitespace-only): the warning reappears for each. The logic must be based on the checkoutConfigured flag (non-empty and starts with https://), not pattern matching on specific strings.
  1. Bridge-unreachable alert toggles with real process management. Bridge running: alert absent, data loads. Bridge stopped (kill the process): alert appears with skeletons. Restarted: alert clears. No mocked transport is allowed. The liveness check must use a genuine GET /api/status request with a short timeout. Verify by physically stopping and starting the bridge process.
  1. Host guard enforces a fixed exact-match positive allowlist in every mode. The guard accepts exactly {"127.0.0.1:" + port, "localhost:" + port} and rejects everything else. Verify with a battery of malicious and held-out variant hosts: Host: localhost.evil.com:8787 → 403; Host: 127.0.0.1.nip.io:8787 → 403; Host: 127.0.0.1:8788 → 403 (wrong port); Host: localhost:8788 → 403 (wrong port); Host: [::1]:8787 → 403; Host: localhost:5173 → 403 in both production and --dev mode; Host: localhost.attacker.com:8787 → 403 (held-out); Host: 127.0.0.1.evil.org:8787 → 403 (held-out); Host: localhost@evil.com:8787 → 403 (held-out); Host: 127.0.0.1:8787 → normal; Host: localhost:8787 → normal. Code review must confirm the implementation is a positive allowlist check (set membership), not a blocklist of known-bad values.
  1. Origin guard rejects any non-allowlisted origin using a positive allowlist. Verify with a diverse array of held-out, non-allowlisted origins: POST /api/build with Origin: https://evil.com → 403; Origin: null → 403; Origin: http://localhost.evil.com → 403; Origin: http://127.0.0.1.evil.com → 403; Origin: https://attacker.example.com → 403 (held-out); Origin: http://192.168.1.1:8787 → 403 (held-out); Origin: http://127.0.0.1:9999 → 403 (held-out); Origin: http://localhost:5174 → 403 (held-out — wrong dev port). Origin: http://127.0.0.1:8787 → processed. No Origin header → processed. Origin: http://localhost:5173 → 403 in production mode; processed when the bridge is started with --dev. Code review must confirm a positive allowlist, not a blocklist.
  1. Path traversal is blocked by generic realpath confinement without disclosure. Path confinement must use the safe_resolve function (unquote, normpath, realpath, prefix check) from §6.6 for all static routes. The following are SECURITY TEST PROBES, not endpoint definitions — they are malicious inputs expected to return 404:
  • GET /site/../../etc/passwd → 404
  • GET /site/%2e%2e/etc/passwd → 404 (URL-encoded dots)
  • GET /site/..%2f..%2f/etc/passwd → 404 (mixed encoding)
  • GET /site/%252e%252e/etc/passwd → 404 (double encoding)
  • GET /site/../content/curriculum.py → 404
  • GET /artifacts/../tools/console.py → 404
  • GET /site/index.html → 200 with correct bytes
  • Held-out: GET /site/....//....//etc/passwd → 404
  • Held-out: GET /site/..%5c..%5c/etc/passwd → 404 (backslash encoding)
  • Held-out: GET /site/%00../etc/passwd → 404 (null byte)
  • Fuzz: generate 50+ additional traversal variants (null bytes, Unicode normalization tricks, ..\..\..\windows\win.ini, triple encoding, path separators in different positions) → all must return 404

Traversal never returns 403 (no existence oracle). The confinement must not pattern-match specific payloads. Code review must confirm safe_resolve with realpath is the only confinement mechanism.

  1. Existing product tests pass unmodified. In a clean checkout with the full console implementation: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . exits 0 with 48 passing tests, verified by an automated script. tools/build.py is byte-identical to its pre-console state.
  1. Bridge and wrapper are stdlib-only. Run under python3 -S in a clean venv: the bridge starts, serves the console, and answers every endpoint without importing non-stdlib code (including via exec/eval/plugin mechanisms).
  1. No customer-facing file changes except config.js. SHA-256 every file under site/ (excluding config.js) and content/ before and after exercising all console operations; hashes match exactly.
  1. Customer site remains functional and unchanged. Serve site/ via python3 -m http.server --directory site before and after console implementation; landing and pack page hashes (excluding expected config.js changes) are identical.
  1. Build lock prevents concurrency under high load (build-vs-build). Spawn 10 simultaneous POST /api/build requests from multiple async workers: exactly one succeeds and the other nine receive HTTP 409 with type: "lock_contention". After completion, a subsequent build succeeds (lock released). Verify the lock is released in a finally block by checking that a crash during build (e.g., killing the bridge mid-build) does not wedge subsequent operations on restart. Code review must confirm a single shared threading.Lock instance, not per-endpoint locks.
  1. Build lock prevents concurrency (build-vs-test, both directions, with overlapping operations). Submit a long-running build (insert time.sleep(5) into build_all() temporarily), then while it runs, submit a test request from a separate client and confirm it receives 409. Then, while a long-running test is in progress (insert time.sleep(5) into a test temporarily), submit a build and confirm 409. Code review must confirm a single shared threading.Lock instance guards both endpoints — not per-endpoint locks with special-case detection.
  1. Timeout kills hung operations via multiple hang scenarios. Test with at least two distinct hang mechanisms: (a) time.sleep(200) in build_all(), (b) an infinite loop while True: pass with no output. Each must be injected separately. For each, the bridge terminates the subprocess at 120 seconds using Popen.terminate() (→ 5s wait → Popen.kill()), returns type: "timeout", releases the lock, and answers the next request normally. Verify by inspecting the process table after the timeout: no Python subprocess with the terminated PID should still be alive; the next request must not encounter residual process interference. Remove the hangs afterward. This must work on both Unix and Windows (no os.kill with signal.SIGTERM).
  1. Pilot reset clears only pilot data and succeeds when stored version > 0. Seed sales (incrementing _version to at least 3) and a build result; reset with the typed-RESET confirmation via POST /api/pilot/reset: pilot-state.json equals the §6.4 defaults (including _version: 0); console-state.json still holds the last build/test; no product file changed. Verify the reset succeeds despite the stored _version being >0 — the POST /api/pilot/reset endpoint bypasses the version check. A PUT /api/pilot with _version: 0 must be rejected as a version conflict, proving the dedicated reset endpoint is necessary. Additionally, verify that pilot-state.json on disk does NOT contain a thresholds field after the reset (thresholds are injected only on GET responses).
  1. Email masking is a general algorithm, not a lookup table. The masking algorithm must split at @ and apply the rules: local length ≥ 3 → first 2 chars + + @ + full domain; else + @ + full domain. Verify with a held-out set of emails whose expected masks are computed offline by a reference implementation: jane.doe@gmail.com → ja***@gmail.com; a@b.co → @b.co; ab@example.org → @example.org (local length 2 < 3); x@y.io → @y.io; john.smith+tag@protonmail.com → jo@protonmail.com; longname.with.dots@sub.domain.com → lo***@sub.domain.com. The console's output must match for all held-out cases. Full addresses appear only in the row detail panel, never in the table.
  1. Accessibility requirements hold across all screen states, verified by both automated and manual testing. Every iframe has a title; every icon-only button has an aria-label; the skip link is the first focusable element and moves focus to main content; focus rings are visible; heading hierarchy is one h1 per page with no skipped levels; disabled buttons show explanatory tooltips. Verify by: (a) automated audit (Lighthouse or axe-core); (b) manual keyboard-only navigation covering every screen state including error alerts (bridge-unreachable, build failure, pilot conflict, config corruption, kill-threshold breach, live-render error in iframe) and dynamic content (modals, accordion expansion, tab switching, sidebar collapse). The manual test must confirm that focus is managed when modals open and close, that all interactive elements in every state are reachable via keyboard, and that heading hierarchy is correct in dynamically rendered content.
  1. Contract badges mirror the test suite, never duplicate it. Break a Module 4 compliance test: the corresponding badge turns red with the failing test name. Temporarily rename a mapped test class: its badge shows gray "Not checked" — never a false green. Restore both.
  1. Curriculum source error is handled gracefully for multiple error types. Introduce at least three different types of errors in content/curriculum.py: (a) a SyntaxError (unmatched parenthesis), (b) an IndentationError (mixed tabs and spaces), (c) a NameError (referencing an undefined variable). For each, GET /api/curriculum returns { ok: false, type: "source_error" } with a stderr excerpt; the Curriculum and Preview screens show a red Alert with the error message and a prompt to fix content/curriculum.py; the Pilot and Launch screens remain fully functional — their API calls (GET /api/pilot, GET /api/config) do not depend on curriculum data and succeed normally. Restore the file: the alert clears and curriculum data loads on the next API call without a bridge restart.
  1. Pilot state corruption recovery works for multiple corruption patterns. Write at least three different corrupt payloads to console/data/pilot-state.json: (a) truncated JSON like { corrupt, (b) non-text binary content, (c) a valid JSON object that lacks the expected keys (e.g., {"foo": "bar"}). For each, GET /api/pilot returns { ok: false, type: "pilot_corrupted" }; the Pilot screen shows the red Alert with "Pilot state file is corrupted. You can reset it to defaults; previous entries will be lost." Click "Reset pilot data" (with the typed-RESET confirmation): the file is replaced with the §6.4 defaults (including _version: 0) via POST /api/pilot/reset; GET /api/pilot succeeds with default values; console-state.json is untouched. Verify by reading the file afterward for each corruption case.
  1. Pilot version conflict prevents silent data loss across multi-step concurrent scenarios. Test multiple overlapping update patterns: (a) Tab A saves once (version N→N+1), tab B with version N saves → 409 with current state including tab A's sale; (b) Tab A saves three times (version N→N+3), tab B with version N saves → 409; (c) Tab A saves, tab B saves and gets 409, reloads, saves again successfully against N+1. In all cases, pilot-state.json contains all saved entries after the sequence; no data is silently lost. The bridge compares _version exactly; any mismatch triggers the conflict. The logic must be generic integer comparison, not based on known version deltas.
  1. Config round-trips through the quoted-key template for multiple input sets. Save at least three different URL/email pairs (with varying characters including braces, special characters, and long values): after each save, verify the file contains double-quoted keys ("checkoutUrl":, "contactEmail":) and that GET /api/config successfully reads the values back without error. The template must always use json.dumps for key and value encoding — quoting is unconditional, not conditional on input. Additionally save a URL containing } and verify round-trip succeeds — the raw_decode parser must handle braces in string values.
  1. Live-render error page is legible HTML, not raw JSON — on all three live routes, for multiple failure types. Trigger at least three distinct failure modes on each of the three live routes (pack HTML, pack PDF, tool preview): (a) SyntaxError in content/curriculum.py, (b) a forced timeout by hanging the render, (c) a deliberate RuntimeError (e.g., raising in a render function). Every combination (3 routes × 3 failure types = 9 cases) must return Content-Type: text/html HTTP 200 with the styled §7.2a error page and the escaped error message — never application/json. Verify by inspecting each response's Content-Type and body (must contain <html and the html.escape()-escaped error message). The iframe must render it correctly. Restore the source; live previews render correctly on the next attempt.
  1. Wrapper sys.path fix resolves product imports. Run python3 tools/console_bridge.py curriculum from the repository root. The wrapper must successfully import content.curriculum and print the curriculum JSON. Verify that sys.path includes the repository root (not just tools/). Without the fix, the wrapper exits with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'content', which the bridge would misattribute as a source_error pointing at curriculum.py.
  1. Freshness detection covers all source files. Touch tools/render_html.py (without touching content/curriculum.py): all packs show as Stale on the Dashboard and Build screens. Touch tools/pdfgen.py: same result. Touch tools/build.py: same result. This verifies the freshness baseline is the max mtime across all five source files, not just curriculum.py.
  1. Cross-platform subprocess termination and executable. Grep tools/console.py and tools/console_bridge.py for os.kill, signal.SIG, and the string 'python3' used as a subprocess executable — no matches. The termination logic uses Popen.terminate() and Popen.kill() exclusively. All subprocess.Popen calls use sys.executable as the first element of the argument list, so on Windows the bridge starts and operates without error (TerminateProcess, not Unix signals; sys.executable, not a PATH-dependent python3).
  1. Build failure response includes best-effort partial artifacts from multiple failure points. Introduce at least two distinct build failures at different stages: (a) a raise after HTML render but before PDF render, (b) a raise after PDF render but before zip bundling. For each, POST /api/build returns { ok: true, data: { ok: false, error, type: "build_failure", artifacts: [...], zips: [...] } } where artifacts and zips are a best-effort filesystem snapshot of whatever exists. The test must independently verify the disk state after the error and compare with the API response arrays — they must match exactly; the returned arrays must reflect the real filesystem state, not pre-baked data. The Build screen displays the red error alert and the partial artifact table showing which packs were generated and which were not. Restore the file after each test.
  1. Bridge creates console/data directory before first write of either state type. Delete console/data/ entirely. Perform a pilot save first (before any build): the bridge must create console/data/ via os.makedirs('console/data', exist_ok=True) before writing pilot-state.json. No FileNotFoundError. Then delete console/data/ again and perform a build or test run: the bridge must create the directory before writing console-state.json. The code must have a single, consistent os.makedirs call before every write path, not just before build/test writes.
  1. Pilot threshold metadata is exposed via API and never persisted. GET /api/pilot returns a thresholds array with five entries (E-001 through E-005), each containing experiment_id, channel, channel_key, success_threshold, kill_threshold, budget_usd, and duration_days. The client renders ChannelCard components from this data. Modify the bridge's static threshold block and confirm the client displays the updated values after a refetch — no client code change required. Verify that pilot-state.json on disk does NOT contain a thresholds field after any PUT operation — the bridge strips it. Perform a PUT with thresholds in the body and confirm the file on disk lacks it.
  1. Bridge verifies wrapper existence at startup. Temporarily rename tools/console_bridge.py to tools/console_bridge.py.bak. Run python3 tools/console.py. The bridge must print a clear error message naming the missing file and exit non-zero. It must not start and serve a broken console.
  1. HTML escaping of error messages in live-render error pages. Introduce a SyntaxError in content/curriculum.py whose error output contains the literal string <script>alert(1)</script> (e.g., a line of raw HTML in the Python source). Request GET /api/packs/{slug}/html?src=live and verify the response body contains the HTML-escaped version (&lt;script&gt;alert(1)&lt;/script&gt;) — not the raw <script> tag. Verify the Content-Type is text/html. Repeat for GET /api/packs/{slug}/pdf?src=live and GET /api/tools/{toolId}. The bridge must use html.escape() from the stdlib on the error text before insertion into the §7.2a template.

Obligation Responses

OBL-1: ADDRESSED — §7.3 defines a dedicated POST /api/pilot/reset endpoint that bypasses the optimistic-concurrency guard entirely (no _version required in the request body, no version check performed) and writes the §6.4 default object with _version: 0 atomically. §10.7 wires the typed-RESET confirmation dialog to this endpoint; the VersionConflictDialog never appears during reset. §4, §5.5, §6.2, §6.4, §12, §13, §15, and §16 all reference the endpoint consistently. AC-27 verifies the reset succeeds when stored _version > 0 AND that a PUT /api/pilot with _version: 0 is rejected as a version conflict — proving the dedicated endpoint is necessary rather than decorative. AC-32 verifies the corruption-recovery reset path through the same endpoint.

OBL-2: ADDRESSED — §7.2a specifies that the bridge calls html.escape(error_message, quote=True) from the Python standard library on the stderr excerpt before inserting it into the HTML error page template, converting & → &amp;, < → &lt;, > → &gt;, " → &quot;, and ' → &#x27;. A complete build_error_page() function is provided showing the escaping call site, and the escaping is performed bridge-side before the HTML string is assembled. The rule applies to all failure types on all three live-render routes. AC-35 verifies text/html + escaped body across 9 route×failure combinations; AC-43 verifies the defense directly by injecting a <script>alert(1)</script> payload into error output and asserting the escaped form in the response.

OBL-3: ADDRESSED — thresholds is never persisted. §6.2 carries a dedicated "Thresholds handling in pilot state" bullet; §6.4 states the file stores only pilot-operational data; §7.5 makes stripping a binding requirement ("The bridge must strip the thresholds field from the PUT request body before writing"); §7.5a specifies always-inject-on-GET from the static config block; §12 notes the client treats thresholds as read-only with bridge-side stripping as the binding requirement; §15 lists persistence of thresholds as an explicit non-goal. AC-41 verifies the file on disk lacks thresholds after a PUT that includes it, and that modifying the bridge's static block changes the GET response with no file change.

OBL-4: ADDRESSED — §7.1 now has two verification tables: function signatures, and a separate module-level constants table listing all seven constants (MODULES, TOOLS, BAND_LABELS, PRODUCT_NAME, PRODUCT_SUBTITLE, PRICE_USD, GUARANTEE_DAYS) with expected location and type. The accompanying text explains the failure mode being prevented: a hallucinated attribute name produces an AttributeError that the bridge would misattribute as type: "source_error" pointing at curriculum.py. The front matter and §7 BINDING NOTE both name this as "function-signature and constant-name verification."

OBL-5: ADDRESSED — §7's BINDING NOTE now reads "The spec contract validator's 117 endpoint_missing findings" (not the earlier incorrect 105), matching the validator's reported count. §16 records the correction in a "Validator finding count" debt entry. The argument — routes are new deliverables, not pre-existing endpoints — is unaffected by the count.

HUNGERHALL — G6 Prototype Spec

Run: gap-253b64a1 · Phase: G6 · Authority: G2 GDD (FROZEN) + G3 Voice Bible (FROZEN) + G4 Art Direction (FROZEN, Palette A) + G5 UX Flow (FROZEN) · Engine: Godot 4.7 (LOCKED) · Platform: Steam (Windows export — export qualification is a later lane)

1. Engine choice

Godot 4.7 is LOCKED by the operator constraint and confirmed in G2's header. G2 §7 freezes a pure-rules architecture (RefCounted objects, single autoload, semantic input/snapshot API, seeded PRNG, fixed 60 Hz) that Godot's Resource system and SceneTree execute natively — no engine friction, no architecture impedance. The GDD's open questions (§10) demand deterministic bot validation across hundreds of runs; Godot's headless main-scene launch with --fixed-fps 60 and ci/sneferu_bot.gd against the shared rules core answers them mechanically. The 2D pixel-art presentation (32px tiles, 640×360 virtual resolution, CanvasModulate life-light system, Control themes) maps directly to Godot's TileMap, CanvasLayer, SpriteFrames, and Theme resources. G7 converges one cooperative run: pure rules in core/, thin projections in scenes/, one bot seam in ci/.

2. Project layout

HUNGERHALL/
  project.godot
  main.tscn
  scripts/
    main.gd                       — entry point; bot-mode handoff; sneferu_primary_action routing
    scene_router.gd               — screen visibility management; transition parameter passing
  core/
    rules_state_machine.gd        — State enum (G2 §1); transition validation; EARS condition checks
    rules_session.gd              — session orchestration; input(action) / snapshot() API; fixed 60Hz tick
    rules_floor.gd                — floor state; tile grid; entity spawn registry; seeded PRNG owner
    rules_player.gd               — player HP; movement at class speed; combat; class potion effects
    rules_enemy.gd                — enemy AI per EnemyDef.ai_type; contact damage; pathfinding on tile grid
    rules_generator.gd            — generator spawn logic; per-generator alive cap (6); per-floor cap (28)
    rules_projectile.gd           — projectile state; collision; pierce/splash logic; Lobber wall-ignore
    rules_hazard.gd               — hazard timing state machine; damage; telegraph; bounce/teleport safety
    rules_score.gd                — score calculation; death penalty (20% flat); floor clear bonus; chest values
    rules_replay.gd               — replay recording and playback; semantic action codec (move_N, attack, etc.)
    save_manager.gd               — save/load; atomic temp-file+rename; version migration; profile persistence
    floor_loader.gd               — FloorData resource loading; missing-floor detection and handling
    seed_prng.gd                  — deterministic PRNG wrapper; integer-seeded; all floor randomness flows through this
  scenes/
    splash.tscn                   — 1.2s Sneferu pipeline mark; skippable after 0.3s; no Back behavior
    title.tscn                    — menu: New Game, Continue (conditional), New Game+ (conditional), Hall of Heroes, Settings, Exit
    class_select.tscn             — four class cards (Warrior pre-highlighted); DESCEND button; Back to title
    play.tscn                     — gameplay root: GameCanvasLayer + UICanvasLayer + OverlayCanvasLayer
    paused.tscn                   — overlay over play: Resume, Settings, Quit to Title
    settings.tscn                 — flat scrollable: Audio, Video, Accessibility, Controls, Game sections
    hall_of_heroes.tscn           — score table; Standard / New Game+ tabs; 8 entries per class
    dying.tscn                    — cinematic crumble (1.2s default / 0.2s reduced motion); no input
    continue_offer.tscn           — 10s ring; YES/NO; token count; 300ms input grace on entry
    game_over.tscn                — final score; inline initials entry; Retry Floor N; Hall of Heroes; Return to Title
    floor_results.tscn            — floor stats (time, kills, food, score); Next Floor; Save and Quit; SAVED tag
    campaign_results.tscn         — campaign stats; inline initials entry; NG+ unlock notice; Return to Title
    floor_missing.tscn            — modal: Back to Title / Skip Floor (F1–23 only; F24 no skip)
  ui/
    hud.tscn                      — HP numeral (32px, top-left); score (32px, top-center); floor (16px, top-right); potions/keys (16px icons, bottom-left)
    announcer_caption.tscn        — caption display; white #FFFFFF on #000000CC; 24px Silkscreen; 2s minimum hold
    plaque_button.tscn            — themed Button: ui_slate fill, text_bone rim, service_amber focus inlay
    clipped_plaque_stylebox.gd    — custom StyleBox for destructive buttons: quarter-circle crescent corner cut
    idle_prompt.tscn              — MOVE / THROW / EXIT glyph overlays; timed fade; tutorial speedrule skip
    initials_entry.tscn           — 3-slot character entry; A–Z only; arcade-style; auto-fires on qualification
    quit_warn.tscn                — modal: "QUIT TO TITLE? FLOOR PROGRESS IS LOST." YES / NO (NO default)
    newgame_warn.tscn             — modal: fires when campaign save exists and New Game / New Game+ chosen
    erase_warn.tscn               — modal: irreversible data wipe confirmation
    reset_warn.tscn               — modal: settings-only reset confirmation
    remap_capture.tscn            — modal: single key/button capture per action row
    credits_pop.tscn              — modal: scrollable credits text
    privacy_pop.tscn              — modal: privacy policy text
    pad_lost.tscn                 — modal: gamepad disconnect; always renders over paused
    save_fail.tscn                — modal: autosave write failed; Retry / Skip Save
  ci/

Binding project.godot requirements for G7:

  • application/run/main_scene = "res://main.tscn"
  • [autoload]: SessionStateMachine="*res://core/rules_state_machine.gd" — the ONLY autoload
  • [input]: sneferu_primary_action bound to physical Space key (keycode 32); throw bound to J, Z, Ctrl, and Space; potion bound to K and east face; pause bound to Esc and Start; move_up/move_down/move_left/move_right bound to WASD, arrows, and left stick
  • rendering/textures/vram_compression/import_etc2_astc = true (binding — controller's macOS packaging requires it; harmless for all projects)
  • physics/common/physics_ticks_per_second = 60
  • physics/common/max_physics_steps_per_frame = 1 (no catch-up; fixed 60 Hz determinism)

3. Module boundaries

scripts/ — Entry point and screen routing

Types: Main (Node, root of main.tscn), SceneRouter (Node, child of Main).

Responsible for: Parsing -- user-arguments for bot mode (--telemetry-out, --games, --seed, --frame-budget); routing sneferu_primary_action to the context-appropriate semantic action (confirm in menus, attack in play); toggling screen visibility via SceneRouter; passing transition parameters between screens.

NOT responsible for: Game rules, state validation, save logic, rendering game world, announcer scheduling.

Public API: Main.enter_bot_mode(args: Dictionary) → invokes ci/sneferu_bot.gd; SceneRouter.show_screen(screen_name: String, params: Dictionary) → sets target screen visible, all others invisible; SceneRouter.get_active_screen() -> String.

core/ — Pure deterministic rules layer

Types: All RefCounted objects. No Node, Control, Node2D, viewport, input, animation, audio, or frame-rate dependency.

rules_state_machine.gd — Owns the G2 §1 state enum: TITLE, CLASS_SELECT, PLAYING, PAUSED, FLOOR_RESULTS, CAMPAIGN_RESULTS, CONTINUE_OFFER, GAME_OVER, DYING. Validates every transition against the G2 §1 transition table. EARS conditions checked: HP ≤ 0 → Dying within 1 physics frame; exit-door overlap 3 consecutive frames + floor < 24 → FloorResults; same + floor == 24 → CampaignResults; continue YES + tokens > 0 → floor rebuild with specified reset values. Public API: request_transition(verb: String) -> bool, current_state() -> State, can_transition(verb: String) -> bool.

rules_session.gd — Session orchestration. Owns a RulesFloor instance and all subordinate rules objects. Accepts semantic input via input(action: Dictionary) where action = {move: Vector2, attack: bool, potion: bool, pause: bool}. Produces complete state via snapshot() -> Dictionary returning {state, hp, score, floor, position, enemies, generators, tokens, food_positions, key_positions, door_positions, exit_position, hazards}. Advances all rules at fixed 60 Hz via tick(delta: float = 1.0/60.0). Public API: input(action), snapshot(), tick(delta), load_floor(floor_data: FloorData, class_def: ClassDef), rebuild_floor_from_baked().

rules_floor.gd — Floor state: tile grid, entity spawn registry, food/key/door/chest positions, hazard spawns. Owns the SeedPRNG instance; all floor-level randomness flows from the floor seed. Public API: tile_at(x, y) -> int, is_walkable(x, y) -> bool, has_los(from, to) -> bool, rng() -> SeedPRNG.

rules_player.gd — Player HP, position, movement at class speed, facing (S/E/N with W as code mirror), combat (throw projectile), potion use, class-specific abilities. Tracks floor-entry score for death penalty calculation. Public API: take_damage(amount: int, source: String), heal(amount: int), move(direction: Vector2, delta: float), throw() -> RulesProjectile, use_potion(), hp_percent() -> float.

rules_enemy.gd — Enemy AI per EnemyDef.ai_type: pursue_wallpass (Ghost: ignores walls), pursue_pathfind (Grunt: A* around walls), maintain_distance (Demon: 4-tile hold + fire), seek_los_gap (Lobber: seeks LOS, lobs over walls), pursue_blink (Sorcerer: blink to LOS tile when HP < 40 + no LOS for 2s, cooldown 5s), pursue_slow (Death: slow pursuit, touch aura). Contact damage per 0.5s tick. Public API: tick(delta: float, floor: RulesFloor, player: RulesPlayer), take_damage(amount: int) -> bool (killed).

rules_generator.gd — Generator spawn logic. Tracks own alive count independently. Blocks own spawning at 6 alive. Blocks when per-floor alive count reaches 28. Spawns at cadence from GeneratorDef. Public API: tick(delta: float, floor: RulesFloor) -> RulesEnemy (or null), take_damage(amount: int) -> bool (destroyed), alive_count() -> int.

rules_projectile.gd — Projectile state: position, velocity, damage, range, pierce flag, splash radius, owner class, wall-collision flag (Lobber ignores walls, collision mask = player hitbox only). Public API: tick(delta: float, floor: RulesFloor) -> bool (expired), on_hit(target) -> int (damage dealt).

rules_hazard.gd — Hazard timing state machine per HazardDef: flame jet (periodic 1.0s on / 2.0s off), void bridge (phased 1.5s walkable / 1.5s void), collapsing void (player-step trigger, 2.0s to removal, permanent). Telegraph states. Bounce/teleport safety for void hazards. Public API: tick(delta: float, floor: RulesFloor, player: RulesPlayer) -> HazardResult.

rules_score.gd — Score calculation. Kill scores per enemy type (Ghost +10, Grunt +25, Demon +40, Lobber +50, Sorcerer +60, Death +200). Generator destroyed +100. Floor clear +500. Campaign clear +2000. Death penalty: 20% of floor-entry score, flat per death, non-compounding. Chest values baked per floor. Public API: on_kill(enemy_type: String), on_generator_destroyed(), on_floor_clear(), on_campaign_clear(), on_death() -> int (penalty), current_score() -> int.

rules_replay.gd — Replay recording: captures seed + ordered semantic actions + version_hash. Playback: feeds semantic actions into RulesSession.input() at the recorded frames. Input strings: move_N, move_NE, move_E, move_SE, move_S, move_SW, move_W, move_NW, attack, potion, pause, resume, quit. Frames with no input are omitted. Public API: start_recording(seed: int, class: String), record_action(frame: int, action: String), stop_recording() -> Dictionary, playback(replay: Dictionary, session: RulesSession).

save_manager.gd — Save/load. Writes ONLY on FloorResults entry (atomic: temp-file + rename). Save schema: {save_version: 1, floor: int, class: String, score: int, potions_remaining: int, ng_plus: bool, timestamp: int}. Migration: unrecognized save_version → fresh start with notification. Profile persistence: NG+ unlock flag and classes_cleared array. Public API: save(session: RulesSession) -> bool, load() -> Dictionary (or null), has_save() -> bool, load_profile() -> Dictionary, save_profile(profile: Dictionary).

floor_loader.gd — Loads FloorData resources from res://Data/floors/floor_NN.tres via ResourceLoader.load(). Missing-floor detection: if resource fails to load, triggers floor_missing modal. Public API: load_floor(floor_num: int) -> FloorData (or null).

seed_prng.gd — Deterministic PRNG wrapper. Integer-seeded. All floor-level randomness (enemy spawn variation, Sorcerer blink destination selection, Death spawn position) flows through this. Public API: seed(seed: int), randi() -> int, randi_range(min, max) -> int, randf() -> float.

scenes/ — Thin Control / Node2D projections

Types: Each .tscn file is a Control or Node2D scene with a script that reads from RulesSession.snapshot() and forwards input to RulesSession.input() or SessionStateMachine.request_transition().

Responsible for: Rendering state from the snapshot; forwarding raw input to the appropriate semantic API; emitting stable semantic cue events (see §7.4); rendering UI per G5 wireframes and G4 style contract.

NOT responsible for: Game rules, state validation, save logic, score calculation, AI behavior, spawn timing. A scene is never a second truth store.

Public API per scene: Each screen script exposes show_screen(params: Dictionary) (called by SceneRouter) and hide_screen(). The play.tscn script additionally exposes is_playing: bool (property for journey contract) and projectile_spawned: bool (property for journey contract).

ui/ — Reusable UI components

Types: Control scenes and one StyleBox subclass.

Responsible for: HUD numerals and icons; announcer caption display with timing; themed buttons with focus/hover/press states; custom destructive-button StyleBox with crescent corner cut; tutorial glyph overlays; initials entry; modal dialogs (quit_warn, newgame_warn, erase_warn, reset_warn, remap_capture, credits_pop, privacy_pop, pad_lost, save_fail).

NOT responsible for: Game state, input routing to rules, score calculation.

Public API: AnnouncerCaption.show_caption(text: String, duration: float); IdlePrompt.show_prompt(word: String); IdlePrompt.dismiss_prompt(word: String); InitialsEntry.get_initials() -> String; PlaqueButton.set_destructured(is_destructive: bool).

ci/ — Bot and visual test infrastructure

Types: SceneTree scripts (not nodes).

sneferu_bot.gd — Bot driver. Invoked by Main in bot mode. Calls SessionStateMachine.session.input(action) with semantic actions and reads SessionStateMachine.session.snapshot() after each action. Fixed 60 Hz, max 21,600 steps per floor (360s). Three policies: greedy-killer (moves toward nearest enemy, attacks), speed-runner (moves toward nearest objective: key → door → exit), survival-router (moves toward food when HP low, otherwise greedy). Timeout: records outcome: "timeout", floor flagged for review. Writes playtest_telemetry_v1 JSON atomically (temp-file + rename) to the orchestrator-provided absolute path. Public API: run(args: Dictionary) where args contains telemetry_out, games, seed, frame_budget.

sneferu_visual.gd — Optional visual capture helper. Never fakes frames in headless mode. Never invoked by the verifier.

sneferu_visible_asset.json — Governed PNG anchor. Keys: schema (sneferu.game.godot-visible-asset/v1), plan_sha256 (supplied by G7 rendered-assets block), resource_uri (res://Assets/Sprites/warrior_main.png), proof_window (first_5_configured_main_scene_frames).

tests/ — Deterministic GDScript test files

Types: GDScript test classes extending RefCounted with assert methods. Run via Godot's headless test runner.

Responsible for: Driving the state machine into each G2 §1 state; exercising every transition; verifying terminal states; testing mechanical guarantees (soft-lock prevention, concurrency caps, continue reset, death penalty, hazard timing, replay determinism, Valkyrie reduction cone, Elf Volley pattern, food formula, chest determinism, fixed timestep).

NOT responsible for: Rendering, audio, haptics, visual feel (those are OP-4).

Public API: Each test file exposes run_all() -> TestResult with pass/fail counts and failure messages.

Data/ — Resource definitions and manifests

Types: Godot Resource (.tres) files and JSON manifests.

Responsible for: Frozen floor layouts, class definitions, enemy definitions, generator definitions, hazard definitions, tuning data, string manifests, announcer audio manifests. All loaded via ResourceLoader.load() at res:// paths.

NOT responsible for: Runtime state mutation. Resources are read-only at runtime.

Assets/ — Game art, audio, replays

Types: PNG sprites, WAV audio, JSON replay, JSON manifests.

Responsible for: All visual and audio assets governed by ASSET_MANIFEST.json and GODOT_IMPORT_MANIFEST.json. Import settings pinned per family: 32px pixel-art textures (filtering OFF, mipmaps OFF, repeat OFF, lossless, straight alpha); audio WAV (loop flags per cue manifest); fonts unfiltered.

NOT responsible for: Game logic, state, or rules.

4. State management approach

HUNGERHALL's core tension — HP draining as the sole clock while the player negotiates three priced routes per room — demands a rules core where every tick is deterministic and every state is reconstructable from (seed, class, ordered actions). The pure RulesSession (RefCounted, no Node dependency) owns floor/player/enemy/generator/hazard/projectile state and advances at a fixed 60 Hz delta. SessionStateMachine (the single autoload) wraps the session, validates transitions against the G2 §1 table, and exposes input()/snapshot() to both the presentation layer and ci/sneferu_bot.gd. Scene scripts in scenes/ read snapshots and forward intent — they never mutate rules. This split serves THIS prototype because the GDD §10 questions (soft-lock prevention, concurrency cap behavior, continue economy, class survival margins) require hundreds of headless bot runs against the exact same rules code the player experiences, and the 60 Hz fixed timestep with integer-seeded PRNG guarantees replay determinism for regression testing.

Architecture layers (mandatory):

  1. Pure simulation Core — core/ contains all rules as RefCounted objects. No rendering, input, animation, audio, or frame-rate imports. RulesSession.input(action: Dictionary) is the single entry point; RulesSession.snapshot() is the single read API. SeedPRNG owns all randomness from the floor seed. Both the main scene and ci/sneferu_bot.gd invoke this exact seam — never a duplicate ruleset.
  1. Application/controller layer — SessionStateMachine (autoload) owns one RulesSession instance, translates InputMap actions into semantic actions during play, validates state transitions, and manages save/load through SaveManager. Receives an injectable clock (always 1.0/60.0). Contains zero rules — it delegates to RulesSession.tick().
  1. Thin projection — scenes/.tscn scripts read snapshot() and render. ui/.tscn components render HUD, captions, buttons, modals. A scene never holds a second copy of game state. Input from the player is forwarded to SessionStateMachine which routes it to RulesSession.input().
  1. Navigation owner — SceneRouter (child of Main) manages screen visibility. SessionStateMachine.request_transition(verb) validates the transition, updates state, and commands SceneRouter to show the target screen. Scenes request transitions; they do not invent them. No view ever calls change_scene directly.

5. Scene/view hierarchy

Main.tscn (configured project main scene; owns startup + bot-mode handoff)
  ├─ SceneRouter (Node; manages screen visibility)
  ├─ Splash (Control — scripts/main.gd routes sneferu_primary_action to skip)
  ├─ Title (Control — menu buttons; attract replay behind logo)
  │   └─ quit_warn (modal — fires on Exit or Back)
  │   └─ newgame_warn (modal — fires when save exists + New Game / NG+ chosen)
  │   └─ credits_pop (modal — scrollable credits)
  ├─ ClassSelect (Control — four class cards; DESCEND; Back)
  ├─ Play (Node2D — projects shared rules core)
  │   ├─ GameCanvasLayer (layer 0)
  │   │   ├─ TileMap (32px tiles; zone-specific TileSet)
  │   │   ├─ PlayerSprite (Sprite2D; SpriteFrames; hero_flame overlay)
  │   │   ├─ Enemies (Node2D container; enemy sprites spawned/managed by rules)
  │   │   ├─ Projectiles (Node2D container; projectile sprites)
  │   │   ├─ Pickups (Node2D container; food, key, potion, chest sprites)
  │   │   ├─ Generators (Node2D container; generator sprites with cloche crescent)
  │   │   ├─ Hazards (Node2D container; hazard sprites)
  │   │   ├─ Particles (Node2D container; smoke and spark particles)
  │   │   └─ CanvasModulate (life-light dimming: ×1.0 / ×0.80 / ×0.62, 400ms crossfade)
  │   ├─ UICanvasLayer (layer 1 — no modulate)
  │   │   └─ HUD (Control — HP numeral, score, floor, potions, keys; ui_slate panels)
  │   ├─ OverlayCanvasLayer (layer 2 — no modulate)
  │   │   ├─ AnnouncerCaption (Control — white on #000000CC; 24px Silkscreen)
  │   │   └─ IdlePrompts (Control — MOVE / THROW / EXIT glyph overlays)
  │   └─ floor_missing (modal — fires when FloorData fails to load)
  ├─ Paused (Control — overlay; Resume, Settings, Quit to Title)
  │   └─ quit_warn (modal — fires on Quit; "QUIT TO TITLE? FLOOR PROGRESS IS LOST.")
  │   └─ pad_lost (modal — gamepad disconnect; always renders over paused)
  ├─ Settings (Control — flat scrollable; Audio, Video, Accessibility, Controls, Game)
  │   └─ erase_warn (modal — data wipe)
  │   └─ reset_warn (modal — settings reset)
  │   └─ remap_capture (modal — key capture)
  │   └─ credits_pop (modal)
  │   └─ privacy_pop (modal)
  ├─ HallOfHeroes (Control — score table; Standard / NG+ tabs; Back)
  ├─ Dying (Control — cinematic crumble; no input; 1.2s default / 0.2s reduced motion)
  ├─ ContinueOffer (Control — 10s ring; YES / NO; token count; 300ms input grace)
  ├─ GameOver (Control — final score; inline initials; Retry Floor N; Scores; Return)
  │   └─ initials_entry (inline — 3-slot; A–Z; auto-fires on qualification)
  ├─ FloorResults (Control — floor stats; Next Floor; Save and Quit; SAVED tag)
  │   └─ save_fail (modal — autosave write failed; Retry / Skip Save)
  └─ CampaignResults (Control — campaign stats; inline initials; NG+ unlock; Return)
      └─ initials_entry (inline — always fires on campaign clear)

5.1 Presentation contract
{
  "schema": "sneferu.game.presentation-contract/v1",
  "dimension": "2D",
  "camera": "top-down",
  "readability_bar": "Player must distinguish hero class silhouette from nearest threat silhouette and read the falling HP numeral as the brightest pixel on screen within one second.",
  "frame_floors": {
    "play_area_ratio_floor": 0.55,
    "contrast_floor": 24,
    "dark_scene_p50": 16
  },
  "orientation": "landscape",
  "ui_regions": [
    {"name": "hp_hud", "rect": [0.00, 0.00, 0.15, 0.12]},
    {"name": "score_hud", "rect": [0.35, 0.00, 0.65, 0.12]},
    {"name": "floor_hud", "rect": [0.85, 0.00, 1.00, 0.10]},
    {"name": "potions_keys_hud", "rect": [0.00, 0.85, 0.20, 1.00]},
    {"name": "announcer_caption", "rect": [0.20, 0.85, 0.80, 1.00]}
  ]
}

presentation_contract.json ships at the project root. The playtest measures letterbox (play_area_ratio_floor ≥ 0.55 — the 640×360 virtual resolution at integer 2× fills 1280×720 with no letterbox; at 3× fills 1920×1080 with no letterbox), contrast (contrast_floor ≥ 24 — text_bone #F3EAD9 on canvas #0B0A13 yields contrast far above this floor), and darkness (dark_scene_p50 = 16 — HUNGERHALL is intentionally dark; the floor_mid #252039 has luminance ~37, but canvas borders and wall areas pull the median lower; 16 is declared honestly for this noir-arcade aesthetic). The ui_regions declare where persistent HUD elements render; the playtest verifies each region actually renders content with measurable contrast.

6. Test plan

6.1 Deterministic state-machine tests

All tests in tests/ are GDScript classes that instantiate RulesSession and SessionStateMachine directly (no rendering), drive the state machine via input() and request_transition(), and assert on snapshot() values. Every test is deterministic — same seed, same actions, same outcome.

Per-state coverage (G2 §1 states):
