6.2 Godot Playtest Contract (machine-verified — fixed-input gate, not advisory)

Machines grade the finished Godot build by hash-copying the exact staged project and launching its configured main scene with Godot 4.7. Source review is not runtime evidence. The project MUST contain these paths (relative to the directory containing project.godot):

project.godot
ci/sneferu_bot.gd
ci/sneferu_visual.gd       # optional visual lane; never fake frames in headless mode
  1. The configured main scene owns the contract wiring. Its production script preloads/calls ci/sneferu_bot.gd, which drives the same engine/state transitions used by the game without UI sleeps or a second toy implementation. ci/sneferu_bot.gd is a shared logic helper, NOT a detached executable that can manufacture telemetry without starting the product. The main-scene path reads ONLY the user-arguments after Godot's -- separator:
--telemetry-out <absolute-json-path> --games <positive-int> --seed <int>
--frame-budget <positive-int>

The harness launches application/run/main_scene with a command equivalent to:

godot --headless --path <project-root> --fixed-fps 60 \
  -- --telemetry-out <absolute-json-path> --games 200 --seed 1 \
  --frame-budget 36000
  1. The main-scene logic contract writes playtest_telemetry_v1 JSON to the requested absolute path. The telemetry JSON MUST be EXACTLY this shape — the machine validator rejects anything missing these keys (this is a HARD contract, not "when the game exposes them"):
{
  "schema": "playtest_telemetry_v1",
  "engine": "godot",
  "engine_version": "<Engine.get_version_info().string, e.g. 4.7-stable (official)>",
  "game": "<short game name>",
  "games_played": <int = games actually started; 1..the --games value>,
  "games_completed": <int = games that ran to an end state; MAY be < games_played
                      if the --frame-budget is exhausted — partial play is valid,
                      but complete at least ~20 real games>,
  "seed": <the --seed int>,
  "levels": [
    { "level_id": "<stable id, e.g. floor number or level name>",
      "plays": <int, times this level/floor was entered across ALL games>,
      "wins":  <int, times it was cleared>,
      "avg_moves_used": <number>,
      "move_limit": <int>,
      "dead_boards": <int, times it reached a no-legal-move state>,
      "out_of_bounds": <int — 3D builds ONLY: bot position samples outside
                        the spec's declared world bounds; REQUIRED on every
                        level row (even when 0) whenever the game is 3D.
                        2D builds OMIT the key entirely> }
  ],
  "notes": ["<string>", "<string>"]
}

HARD RULES the validator + report depend on:
— engine_version = Engine.get_version_info().string (do not hardcode it).
— 3D builds sample every bot's position against the spec's declared world bounds and report out_of_bounds per level — the harness names any positive count (the fell-through-the-floor detector). Never omit the counter from a 3D build; never invent it for a 2D one. — levels is a PER-LEVEL AGGREGATE array — aggregate your per-game results BY LEVEL/FLOOR (one row per level with plays+wins summed across all games). Do NOT emit one row per game. At least one level MUST have plays > 0. The fun-metrics difficulty curve is scored from plays/wins per level. Each row requires a unique non-empty level_id, plays, wins, avg_moves_used, move_limit, and dead_boards; the harness derives overall win/dead-board rates from these bound rows. — avg_moves_used and move_limit MUST share BOTH the same unit AND the same scope, and notes MUST state which unit that is. The harness derives headroom = (move_limit — avg_moves_used) / move_limit and reports slack/tension from it, so any mismatch silently rewrites the difficulty read. Two mismatches to check for explicitly, because both stay invisible while a coincidence holds:

  • UNIT — a per-input counter divided by a per-tick cap. If your bot happens to emit one input per tick these agree today and diverge the first time it idles, with nothing in the report to show it moved.
  • SCOPE — a per-GAME total measured against a per-TAKE / per-attempt cap (or vice versa). Pick one scope and use it on both sides. If the level's real budget is a clock, report both numbers in ticks and say so; if it is a move count, report both in moves. Do not derive one from the other. — notes MUST be a JSON ARRAY of strings — never a bare string (a bare string is rendered one character per line by the report). — seed must equal the --seed value (or provide a seeds array that includes it). Write through a temporary sibling and rename only after the JSON is complete. Missing or invalid telemetry is a product FAIL and receives a bounded code repair; the artifact is still preserved.

HUNGERHALL telemetry specifics: game = "hungerhall". levels aggregates per floor (level_id = floor number string, e.g. "floor_01"). avg_moves_used and move_limit are both in ticks (60 Hz physics steps) — move_limit = 21,600 (360s cap per floor). notes states: "unit: ticks at 60 Hz; scope: per floor attempt; move_limit = 21600 ticks = 360s". dead_boards = count of floor attempts where the bot reached a no-legal-move state (HP > 0 but no path to exit — should be 0 if solver is correct). This is a 2D build — out_of_bounds is OMITTED entirely.

  1. Godot import and script checks must be clean. The harness runs an editor import of the project and checks ci/sneferu_bot.gd in that project context before main-scene execution. Do not depend on editor-global plugins, absolute developer paths, or unpinned custom addons.
  1. Rendered assets live below res://Assets/. Read Assets/ASSET_MANIFEST.json (and the Godot delivery manifest when present) through FileAccess/ResourceLoader; do not hardcode imported-cache paths below .godot/imported. Every shipped asset must be manifest-loaded or explicitly referenced by a scene/script/resource. When the delivery plan contains a product-qualified PNG texture, the configured main scene MUST display at least one such governed texture during its first five fixed-fps MovieWriter frames. Bind that anchor through its exact res://Assets/... URI in a scene/script/resource; it may not be hidden, fully transparent, off-canvas, replaced by a placeholder, or deferred behind operator input. Write ci/sneferu_visible_asset.json as the one authoritative anchor with exactly these keys: schema, plan_sha256, resource_uri, and proof_window. The schema is sneferu.game.godot-visible-asset/v1; resource_uri is the exact governed PNG URI you visibly place; proof_window is first_5_configured_main_scene_frames; and the G7 rendered-assets block supplies the exact current plan_sha256. Do not select a store capsule. The verifier changes only that texture in an evidence copy and requires the rendered pixels to change before it can claim generated art is in use. When the delivery plan contains a product-qualified mesh_3d GLB, the configured main scene MUST also instantiate at least one such governed mesh visibly during the same first five frames. Write ci/sneferu_visible_mesh.json with the same four exact keys, schema sneferu.game.godot-visible-mesh/v1, today's exact plan_sha256, the actually visible res://Assets/...glb URI, and proof window first_5_configured_main_scene_frames. The verifier collapses only that GLB's position geometry in an evidence copy and requires rendered pixels to change. A loaded-but-hidden mesh does not satisfy this contract.

A shader-input map is DATA, not art — never render one directly. A manifest row whose category is shader_texture, or whose purpose describes CHANNELS rather than a picture (noise/threshold/mask/field/atlas, "R = ...", "G = ...", "packed ... patterns"), exists to be SAMPLED by a shader. Satisfy its reference requirement by binding it to a sampler2D uniform on a ShaderMaterial that something actually uses — that is a real reference and the usage scan counts it. Do not discharge the requirement by assigning it to a Sprite3D, TextureRect, Decal, or any other visible node: its channels are not a composed image, so it renders as garbage. This is a measured failure mode, not a style note. Such a map may never be the visible governed-PNG anchor above. If no shader in the build samples it, say so in Known Blockers and leave it unrendered: an honestly-declared unconsumed asset is a finding, and a lookup map painted onto the stage is a defect.

HUNGERHALL: 2D build — no mesh_3d GLB, no ci/sneferu_visible_mesh.json. The governed PNG anchor is res://Assets/Sprites/warrior_main.png (the Warrior sprite sheet, displayed when the player enters play on floor 1). ci/sneferu_visible_asset.json:

   {
     "schema": "sneferu.game.godot-visible-asset/v1",
     "plan_sha256": "<supplied by G7 rendered-assets block>",
     "resource_uri": "res://Assets/Sprites/warrior_main.png",
     "proof_window": "first_5_configured_main_scene_frames"
   }
  1. ci/sneferu_visual.gd is an optional product helper, never capture authority. The verifier does not trust or invoke product-authored capture code. FIX-790 (2026-07-30) originally ran the configured main scene with nobody pressing anything, which honestly observed startup but could never show the gameplay that G8 must judge.

The harness now owns both bounded MovieWriter modes in the godot_visual_product_capture step. It always runs the project's configured main scene from an evidence copy. When the product ships a regular journey_contract.json, the GAME playtest path adds the exact repository-owned godot_journey_driver.gd; that driver loads the configured scene and dispatches only the contract's declared InputEventActions. With no contract, or with godot_visual_journey_drive=false, capture remains input-free:

   godot --path <evidence-copy> --display-driver <d> --rendering-method <r>
         --audio-driver Dummy --windowed --resolution <declared WxH>
         --write-movie <prefix> --fixed-fps 60 --quit-after <frames>

The journey-aware form appends only:

   --script <repository>/orchestrator/game/godot_journey_driver.gd

This is machine-driven render evidence, not independent human play. It may prove that the declared journey is visible; it may never claim independent capture or independent gameplay proof. The separate external-input replay lane owns those claims. Missing display capability is infrastructure debt, not a reason to stop construction.

  1. The at-rest opening and the declared gameplay journey are both visual evidence. The default journey capture preserves the opening before it injects the first declared action, then records the actual play surface. A static title card is a quality observation, not a reason to hide gameplay from G8 or halt construction. A fully static capture after declared actions is still reported as static_frames, because that means the journey did not produce observable pixels.

Do not add frame-wide pulses, lighting swings, or decorative motion merely to clear a pixel-delta threshold. That is evidence theatre, can reduce the actual art quality, and can create a photosensitivity hazard. Motion should come from the game's real presentation and gameplay. If the opening uses animation, keep it at or below 3 Hz and honour the G5 reduced-motion / accessibility setting. Never branch on OS.has_feature("movie"), a capture flag, or any "am I being recorded" test.

A still first frame is a product finding, repairable in place — never a reason to stop construction and never a substitute for capturing gameplay.

  1. The real configured player journey must survive two external primary actions. project.godot defines sneferu_primary_action with a physical Space binding, and the ordinary configured main scene — not ci/, a hidden test mode, or product-authored evidence code — handles it. Starting from a fresh launch:

— the first action must produce a visible entry transition (for example splash/title to the start surface or directly into play);
— the second action must produce a distinct visible gameplay transition (for example activating the default Start control, beginning the level, or performing the primary mechanic after direct entry); — when a menu is present, its primary/start control has keyboard focus and activates from the same action without requiring a mouse.

Each press edge advances at most one application transition. The product must not observe one injected press through both an event callback and a per-frame is_action_just_pressed poll, nor let a newly mounted screen reuse the still-live edge. Every intermediate step expectation is product truth: reaching the terminal state after skipping Title or Class Select is not a clean journey. Centralize semantic input consumption and require a release followed by a new edge before the next screen transition.

The host runs paired no-input and treatment processes, injects both actions outside the Godot process, and captures the real window before, between, and after them. A single changed splash/menu frame is not gameplay proof. Product failure receives bounded in-place code repair; unavailable GUI or capture authority is evidence debt and never stops construction.

The contract is a MACHINE file with a fixed schema — do not invent one. Write it to the PROJECT ROOT as journey_contract.json (a copy under data/ is never read: the harness opens <project_root>/journey_contract.json and reports contract_missing, skipping the whole rung). Its sibling presentation_contract.json is read from the project root the same way.

6.3 Journey contract

journey_contract.json ships at the project root. Schema game_journey_v1. The harness probe injects the declared InputMap actions through Godot's real input path and evaluates predicates itself.

{
  "schema": "game_journey_v1",
  "entry_wait_frames": 45,
  "steps": [
    {
      "action": "sneferu_primary_action",
      "hold_frames": 3,
      "wait_frames": 45,
      "expect": [
        {"kind": "property_equals", "path": "/root/Main/Title", "property": "visible", "value": true},
        {"kind": "property_equals", "path": "/root/Main/Splash", "property": "visible", "value": false}
      ]
    },
    {
      "action": "sneferu_primary_action",
      "hold_frames": 3,
      "wait_frames": 45,
      "expect": [
        {"kind": "property_equals", "path": "/root/Main/ClassSelect", "property": "visible", "value": true},
        {"kind": "property_equals", "path": "/root/Main/Title", "property": "visible", "value": false}
      ]
    },
    {
      "action": "sneferu_primary_action",
      "hold_frames": 3,
      "wait_frames": 60,
      "expect": [
        {"kind": "property_equals", "path": "/root/Main/Play", "property": "visible", "value": true},
        {"kind": "property_equals", "path": "/root/Main/ClassSelect", "property": "visible", "value": false},
        {"kind": "property_equals", "path": "/root/Main/Play", "property": "is_playing", "value": true}
      ]
    },
    {
      "action": "sneferu_primary_action",
      "hold_frames": 3,
      "wait_frames": 30,
      "expect": [
        {"kind": "property_equals", "path": "/root/Main/Play", "property": "projectile_spawned", "value": true}
      ]
    }
  ],
  "terminal": {
    "audio_cue_required": false,
    "expect": [
      {"kind": "node_exists", "path": "/root/Main/Play"},
      {"kind": "property_equals", "path": "/root/Main/Play", "property": "is_playing", "value": true}
    ]
  }
}

Journey walk: Fresh launch → splash (45 frame entry wait) → Space skips splash to Title (Title.visible=true, Splash.visible=false) → Space activates NEW GAME (default focus, no save on first boot) → ClassSelect appears → Space activates DESCEND (Warrior pre-highlighted) → Play begins (Play.visible=true, is_playing=true, floor 1 loads, Warrior at entrance tile, HP=800, HP drain ticking) → Space fires first throw (projectile_spawned=true, axe spawned along facing). Terminal: Play node exists, is_playing=true. audio_cue_required is false — authored audio arrives after the build.

Node path stability: All screens are children of Main with stable node names. SceneRouter toggles visible (a built-in CanvasItem property). is_playing and projectile_spawned are custom @export var properties on the Play scene script, set when the rules core enters PLAYING state and when the first projectile spawns respectively. The harness probe reads these through Godot's Node.get_indexed() path resolution.

6.4 GDD §10 open questions cross-reference

The GDD §10 open questions (reconstructed from evidence in G2 §1, §3, §7, and the Valkyrie damage reduction specification which references "both aim schemes tested in §10 Q2"):

§10 QuestionTest that answers itHow
Q1: Does the continuous HP-drain clock create genuine three-way price negotiation (direct/greedy/suppression) across all four classes?test_combat.gd + bot telemetry win_rate per classVerifies all 4 class combat signatures produce viable kill rates; bot telemetry compares class win rates across floors; a class with 0% win rate proves a balance defect, not the core promise
Q2: Which aim scheme (auto-aim at nearest vs. manual directional) better serves the Valkyrie's lane-walker identity?test_valkyrie_reduction.gd (runs both schemes)Tests the ±30° threat-anchored cone under both aim schemes; verifies identical behavior (cone is anchored to threat direction, not facing); bot survival rate comparison between schemes answers "which serves better"
Q3: Can any baked floor configuration soft-lock the player (HP > 0 but no path to exit)?test_softlock_prevention.gd + test_floor_solver.gdAll 6 G2 §1 softlock guarantees verified on all 6 shipped floors; solver gates 1–9 checked; no state where HP > 0 and no transition possible
Q4: Does the per-generator alive cap (6) prevent the speedrun exploit without creating dead states?test_concurrency_caps.gdPer-generator cap enforced independently; room A fill does not suppress room B; generators resume spawning after kills; per-floor cap (28) bounds total concurrency
Q5: Is the continue economy (2 tokens/floor, 50% HP, −20% death penalty) fair enough to feel arcade-authentic?test_continue_reset.gd + test_death_penalty.gd + bot telemetryContinue reset verified (HP 50%, potions 0, keys 0, food not restored, generators full, door state preserved); death penalty arithmetic verified (20% flat, non-compounding); bot continue rate and post-continue completion rate measured
Q6: Does the food formula provide sufficient survival margin for the Wizard (520 HP) across all bands?test_food_formula.gd + test_floor_solver.gd (gate 7)Food pieces per band = formula output; Wizard ≥52 HP remaining at exit verified per band; static HP budget check on all shipped floors
Q7: Can the collapsing void or other hazards trap the player in an unwinnable state?test_hazard_timing.gd + test_softlock_prevention.gd (guarantee 5) + test_floor_solver.gd (gate 8)Collapsing-void removal timing verified; bounce/teleport safety verified; solver checks critical path requires no backtracking over collapsed tiles + every collapsible region retains valid bounce/teleport target
Q8: Does the 28-enemy concurrency ceiling hold at 60fps, and is the game deterministic?test_fixed_timestep.gd + test_replay_determinism.gd + headless smoke testFixed 60 Hz verified (no wall-clock dependency); replay determinism (same seed + actions → identical outcome); headless 60s smoke test runs 200 bot games at 28-enemy ceiling without crash

Headless 60-second smoke test (binding): The exact Godot command:

godot --headless --path <project-root> --fixed-fps 60 -- \
  --telemetry-out <absolute-json-path> --games 200 --seed 1 --frame-budget 36000

This launches the configured main scene (main.tscn), which enters bot mode, invokes ci/sneferu_bot.gd against the shared RulesSession core, runs 200 games across the 6 shipped floors with three bot policies, and writes playtest_telemetry_v1 JSON atomically. The smoke test passes if: (a) Godot launches without crash, (b) telemetry is schema-valid with games_played ≥ 20, (c) at least one level has plays > 0, (d) dead_boards is 0 on all floors (solver guarantees no soft-locks), (e) engine_version matches Engine.get_version_info().string.

7. Vertical slice scope

7.1 IN scope for production vertical slice
  • All mechanics needed for the locked core promise: — Continuous HP drain as the sole game clock (drain HP/s per band, G2 §3 table) — 8-way movement at class speed; step puffs every 12px — Manual aimed throws (projectile along current facing, spawned on press frame) — 4 playable classes: Warrior (axe, pierce, whirlwind), Valkyrie (spear, aegis, ±30° reduction), Wizard (bolt, splash, nova), Elf (arrow, 3.0/s, volley) — 6 enemy types with full AI: Ghost (wall-pass), Grunt (pathfind), Demon (maintain-distance + projectile), Lobber (LOS-gap + wall-ignore projectile), Sorcerer (blink), Death (slow pursuit + touch aura) — Generators with per-generator alive cap (6) and per-floor alive cap (28), independent tracking — 3 hazard types: flame jet (periodic), void bridge (phased), collapsing void (player-step, permanent) — Potions: carryable, cap 3, carried between floors, zeroed on continue, class-specific effects — Keys and doors: in-floor pickups, consumed by their door, no interact button — Food: eaten on contact for +150 HP, cannot be banked — Treasure chests: baked values (100/250/500), printed on open frame — Continue system: 2 tokens per floor entry, 10s ring, 50% HP on continue, food not restored — Death penalty: −20% of floor-entry score, flat per death, non-compounding — Save system: autosave on FloorResults entry only, atomic write, migration — Score table: local, 8 entries per class, Standard + NG+ tabs, 3-letter initials
  • Enough bounded content to prove progression and replayability: — 6 floors: F1 (tutorial), F2 (key/door), F3 (potions/treasure), F6 (zone-1 capstone), F7 (Lobber + flame jets), F24 (finale: Death + 3 generators + sealing exit + collapsing void) — All 4 zones represented: Drowned Vaults (F1–6), Cindercrypt (F7), The Hollow Throne (F24) — NG+ applied to the same 6 floors with retuned parameters (enemy HP ×1.5, spawn rate ×1.3, food −20%, drain +0.5 HP/s) — code path and parameter application IN; second baked floor set with different seeds OUT — F1 first-30-seconds path playable exactly as boarded (G2 §3): T+0 spawn + entry bark + HP falling; T+4 MOVE prompt; T+10 THROW prompt; T+15 first kill; T+25 generator burst; T+30 food beat
  • Full state machine implemented: All 9 G2 §1 states (Title, ClassSelect, Playing, Paused, FloorResults, CampaignResults, ContinueOffer, GameOver, Dying) with every transition in the G2 §1 table. All G5 screens and modals reachable.
  • All G5 screens: splash, title (with/without save/NG+ variants), class_select, play, paused, settings (flat scrollable — audio, video, accessibility, controls, game), hall_of_heroes, dying, continue_offer, game_over, floor_results, campaign_results, floor_missing. All G5 modals: quit_warn, newgame_warn, erase_warn, reset_warn, remap_capture, credits_pop, privacy_pop, pad_lost, save_fail. Inline elements: initials_entry, idle_prompts.
  • Primary-journey settings/save behavior: Settings (audio sliders, fullscreen, resolution, reduced motion, screen shake, freeze frames, font size, auto-fire/easy mode, rumble, remap controls, reset scores, delete save) — all on one flat scrollable screen per G5 DIS-4. Save/load (autosave on FloorResults, Continue from title, migration on unrecognized version). Accessibility floor: color-blind safe palette, one-handed playability (remapping + auto-fire), font-size minimums, reduced-motion option, no audio dependency (captions on every announcer line, visual telegraphs for all hazards), haptics opt-out.
  • Minimum complete feel floor: At least three named juice moments (see §7.3), every input acknowledged within 100ms, production-readable UI (themed Control components with Palette A tokens, Silkscreen font, plaque buttons with focus/hover/press states).
  • Primary-journey governed art: Warrior, Valkyrie, Wizard, Elf sprite sheets (32px, 6 frames each); 6 enemy sprites; generator sprite; 4 projectile sprites; food, key, 4 potion, chest, door, exit sprites; hero_flame overlay; 4 zone tilesets; smoke and spark particles. All governed by ASSET_MANIFEST.json and loaded through ResourceLoader at res:// paths.
  • Real audible product audio: Operator-covered cues (see §7.4 Post-build musician handoff). Stable named semantic cue events emitted from the SAME real controller/rules path used by player actions and terminal outcomes. Replaceable no-op hooks. Compact musician handoff manifest mapping cue ID to meaning and callsite. No synthesized placeholders, no downloaded/unknown-origin media, no requirement for audio_playing or AUDIO_PRODUCT_MANIFEST.json before authored audio is supplied.
  • Balance sim runs in tests: Bot runs (greedy-killer, speed-runner, survival-router) across all 6 floors and all 4 classes. Telemetry tracks win_rate, dead_board_rate, avg floor time, continue rate, per-class survival.
7.2 OUT of scope for prototype / production slice
  • Exhaustive content: Floors F4–5, F8–11, F13–17, F19–23 (18 floors not shipped). Full second baked NG+ floor set with different seeds (NG+ parameter application on the 6 shipped floors is IN).
  • Attract replay recording: The replay playback code is IN; the recorded attract replay file (res://Assets/Replays/attract.replay) is OUT for the prototype (title uses a live deterministic bot simulation per G5 attract replay note — or a static title card if live sim is not ready).
  • Unprovisioned infrastructure: Steam achievements, Steam Cloud sync, Steam overlay handling (beyond OS focus-loss auto-pause), online leaderboards, friend comparison, analytics, telemetry services.
  • Downloaded/unknown-origin/unmanifested media: No external audio, no external sprites, no copyrighted images, no Lorem Ipsum.
  • Undeclared dependencies: No third-party Godot addons, no editor-global plugins, no absolute developer paths.
  • IAP, ads, premium currency, DLC: None. G2 §4 is the whole truth.
  • Polish: Exhaustive ornamental effects not tied to the locked identity. Post-process bloom, screen-space glow, per-pixel dynamic lighting, real-time shadows, normal maps, anti-aliased rescaling, gradient fills, parallax, sprite rotation, floating dust motes, ornamental fantasy filigree — all refused per G4.
  • Unqualified export claims: Steam Windows export is a later qualification lane. No export receipt is claimed in this prototype.
  • Final musician-owned production audio: Arrives via the post-build handoff (§7.4). Not required before authored audio is supplied.
  • Dedicated tutorial screen: G2 contracts zero tutorial screens. Teaching rides in-play idle prompts only.
  • Restart Floor button: No restart transition exists in the G2 §1 state machine. Prescribed restart path: Quit to Title → Continue (free, no token consumed).
7.3 Feel & first-party framework contract

1. Engine-native frameworks over hand-rolled substitutes.

HUNGERHALL uses Godot 4.7's native systems exclusively:

  • State machine: SessionStateMachine (autoload) wraps a custom State enum with validated transitions — no AnimationNodeStateMachine or third-party FSM addon. The transition table is small (9 states, 15 transitions) and a custom validator matches the G2 §1 table exactly.
  • Seeded RNG: SeedPRNG wraps Godot's RandomNumberGenerator with an injected integer seed. All floor randomness flows through this.
  • Input: Godot InputMap actions (sneferu_primary_action, throw, potion, pause, move_*). The main scene's _input() translates to semantic actions for RulesSession.input().
  • Tween/AnimationPlayer: Godot Tween for UI transitions (plaque button press offset, caption fade, focus inlay). AnimationPlayer for sprite frame swaps (walk bob, throw arm, generator cloche cycle, hero flame grade swap).
  • Control themes: One Theme resource (res://Themes/hungerhall_theme.tres) binding all Control roles per G4 UI style contract.
  • Audio: Godot AudioStreamPlayer buses for music, effects, announcer. No runtime TTS. Pre-recorded .wav clips loaded via ResourceLoader.
  • CanvasModulate: Godot CanvasModulate on GameCanvasLayer for life-light dimming (×1.0/×0.80/×0.62, 400ms crossfade via Tween).
  • Particles: GPUParticles2D for smoke and spark effects with stepped luminance textures.
  • TileMap: Godot TileMap with zone-specific TileSet resources for 32px tile rendering.

2. Named juice budget — at least THREE juice moments, each specced as event → response(s) → tunable constants in Tunables.json.

#EventResponse(s)Tunable constants
J1Generator destroyed(a) 4-frame freeze (engine get_tree().paused for 4 physics ticks); (b) 2px camera kick (Tween, easeOut, 100ms); (c) smoke particle burst (5–8 particles, wall_body-tinted, normal blend, 600ms upward drift); (d) +100 score floater (Tween upward 40px, easeOut, 500ms); (e) announcer bark with caption (2s hold); (f) HUD rim flash (service_amber, 2-frame pulse)juice_generator_freeze_frames (4, band [0,8], step 1); juice_generator_camera_kick_px (2, band [0,6], step 1); juice_generator_particle_count (6, band [3,12], step 1); juice_generator_floater_duration_ms (500, band [200,1000], step 50)
J2Enemy killed(a) 2-frame white hit flash (sprite self_modulate to white, 2 physics ticks); (b) sprite pop (scale 1.0→1.15→0.0 via Tween, easeOut, 200ms total); (c) +score floater (Tween upward 30px, easeOut, 400ms); (d) 3–5 zone-tinted smoke particles (normal blend, 400ms drift)juice_enemy_hit_flash_frames (2, band [0,4], step 1); juice_enemy_pop_duration_ms (200, band [100,400], step 20); juice_enemy_particle_count (4, band [2,8], step 1); juice_enemy_floater_duration_ms (400, band [200,800], step 50)
J3Food pickup(a) HP tick-up (3×50 over 0.3s, displayed as rolling numeral increment); (b) "FOOD" caption (24px Silkscreen, white on #000000CC, 2s hold); (c) food sprite vanish (scale to 0, easeIn, 100ms); (d) screen-edge amber pulse (1-frame, OverlayCanvasLayer)juice_food_hp_tick_count (3, band [1,5], step 1); juice_food_hp_tick_duration_ms (300, band [100,600], step 50); juice_food_caption_hold_s (2.0, band [1.0,4.0], step 0.25)

Additional juice moments (beyond the minimum three):

  • Hero death (J4): sprite scales to 0 over 200ms (Tween, easeIn); 5–8 smoke particles (wall_body-tinted, normal blend, 600ms upward drift); hero flame detaches and floats up as fading service_amber spark (Tween, 800ms); full presentation spans 1200ms. Tunable: juice_death_crumble_ms (1200, band [200,2000], step 100).
  • Floor clear (J5): results panel slides in (Tween, easeOut, 300ms); floor clear jingle (semantic cue cue.floor_cleared); +500 floater. Tunable: juice_floor_clear_panel_ms (300, band [150,600], step 50).
  • Potion use (J6): 6-frame freeze; class-specific effect animation (Whirlwind radial expansion, Aegis shield ring, Nova radial burst, Volley 12-arrow spawn); HUD potion icon flash. Tunable: juice_potion_freeze_frames (6, band [2,10], step 1).

Every Tween in the plan carries a timing mode (easeOut, easeIn, or easeInOut — never linear-only). Linear motion is a violation of this contract.

EventHapticReason

All haptics are supplemental; no information is absent from visual or audio per G2 §8.6. Master rumble toggle + 0/50/100% intensity steps in Settings. When off, no rumble events fire.

4. Chrome quality floor.

Godot themed Control containers over the game scene. hungerhall_theme.tres binds: Button (ui_slate fill, text_bone 2px border, service_amber focus inlay, 1px pressed offset, diagonal slash for disabled, ClippedPlaqueStyleBox for destructive); Panel (ui_slate fill, optional 1px text_bone border); Label (text_bone, font size per type scale: 8/16/24/32px); TextureProgressBar (critical_brick fill, wall_body background, segmented vertical bar with 1px gaps); HSlider/VSlider (wall_body track, service_amber 8px handle); OptionButton (Button styling + chevron glyph); LineEdit (ui_slate fill, service_amber border, 3-char limit, ALL CAPS); ScrollContainer (ui_slate background); TabContainer (tab bars use Button styling).

Palette tokens from G4 Palette A: canvas #0B0A13, floor_mid #252039, wall_body #191526, wall_cap #5A4E76, text_bone #F3EAD9, ui_slate #16111F, service_amber #F2A23B, critical_brick #D94836, food_gold #EFC258, key_silver #D9DEE2, spectral_cyan #79D6C9, hero class tokens, zone accent tokens.

Pressed/focus/hover states per G4 UI interaction states. Safe-area handling: all critical elements inside 90% centered safe area. Readable target sizes: minimum interactive height 32px physical (16px virtual × 2 at 1280×720). Stable machine-input identifiers: every interactive Control has a stable node name (e.g., btn_new_game, btn_continue, btn_descend, btn_resume, btn_next_floor) usable by the journey probe and future replay systems.

No raw label-as-button hacks: every clickable element is a themed Button or TextureButton with the plaque StyleBox.

5. Every input acknowledged within 100ms.

InputAcknowledgmentLatency
Move (WASD / arrows / left stick)Sprite walk-bob animation starts next physics tick; step puff particle every 12px≤17ms (1 tick)
Throw (J / Z / Ctrl / Space / south face / RT)Muzzle flash (1 frame) + projectile spawned on press tick; 3-frame arm pose; light haptic (if enabled)≤17ms
Potion (K / east face / RB)6-frame freeze; effect application; HUD potion icon flash; medium haptic (if enabled)≤17ms
Pause (Esc / Start)Paused screen renders next tick; drain stops; bark queue freezes≤17ms
Menu navigation (arrows / stick)Focus highlight (service_amber 2px inlay) moves to next control, 100ms fade in≤17ms state change; ≤100ms visual fade
Menu confirm (Enter / A / Space)Button pressed animation (1px down, amber inlay flood 100ms) + state transition≤17ms state change; ≤100ms visual
Pickup (food / key / potion / chest) — overlapSprite vanish + floater + caption + audio cue on overlap tick≤17ms

All gameplay inputs are processed in the fixed 60 Hz physics loop, so gameplay input latency is 1 tick (16.67ms). Menu transitions change state immediately; visual animation may take up to 100ms but the state change is observable on the next tick.

7.4 Post-build musician handoff — non-blocking

The operator is this game's musician and will add finished music and sound effects after a playable game exists. This is a binding G7 implementation requirement.

  • Emit stable, named semantic cue events from the SAME real controller/rules path used by player actions and terminal outcomes. The RulesSession and scene controllers emit signals (Godot Signal) with stable names at the exact callsite where the event occurs. These are the musician's connection points.
  • Provide compact replaceable no-op hooks. Each cue signal connects to a no-op handler by default. When the musician supplies audio, they replace the no-op with an AudioStreamPlayer.play() call. No code change required — just resource assignment.
  • Do not synthesize, download, or add placeholder/dummy audio. Do not require audio_playing, audio_cue_required, audible PCM, or Audio/AUDIO_PRODUCT_MANIFEST.json before authored audio is supplied.
  • Missing audio or PCM is NOT gameplay failure, repair authority, phase admission, or a reason to halt/discard the staged game. The exact post-audio tree will receive the audio qualification rung later.

8. Definition of prototype done

THREE automatable pass criteria. EACH must be machine-verifiable — the cooperative loop gates on them mechanically. None can be "operator plays for 10 minutes" (that is OP-4, the operator gate AFTER G7).

Criterion 1: State-machine tests pass

What: All tests in tests/ pass via Godot's headless test runner. Every G2 §1 state is driven into, every transition is exercised, every terminal state's results are verified. All mechanical tests (soft-lock prevention, concurrency caps, continue reset, death penalty, hazard timing, replay determinism, Valkyrie reduction, Elf Volley, food formula, chest determinism, fixed timestep, save migration) pass.

How it is automatable: godot --headless --path <project-root> --script res://tests/run_all_tests.gd exits with code 0 if all tests pass, non-zero on any failure. Output includes per-test pass/fail counts and failure messages. No human judgment required.

Pass condition: Exit code 0. All 16 test files pass. Zero failures.

Criterion 2: Balance sim runs clean

What: The bot balance simulation (ci/sneferu_bot.gd) runs 200 games across all 6 shipped floors and all 4 classes with three bot policies (greedy-killer, speed-runner, survival-router). Results show: no soft-locks (dead_boards = 0 on all floors), no dominant strategy above 30pp win-rate gap between best and worst class, and avg floor times within the G2 §3 target bands (adjusted for bot skill — bots are minimum-skill agents, so floor times above target are acceptable; floor times below target by >50% indicate the floor is too easy).

How it is automatable: The headless Godot command writes playtest_telemetry_v1 JSON with per-level plays, wins, avg_moves_used, move_limit, dead_boards. A post-processing script validates: dead_boards = 0 for all levels; win_rate per class within [0.10, 0.90] (no class is broken or dominant); games_played ≥ 20. The script exits 0 on pass, non-zero on fail.

Pass condition: Telemetry JSON is schema-valid. dead_boards = 0 on all 6 floors. games_played ≥ 20. No class has 0% win rate across all floors. Win-rate spread between best and worst class ≤ 60pp (not a hard 30pp — the prototype accepts provisional balance; the tuner tightens this after the build).

Criterion 3: Headless 60s smoke launches without crash

What: The configured main scene (main.tscn) launches in headless bot mode, invokes ci/sneferu_bot.gd against the shared RulesSession core, runs for at least 60 seconds (3,600 frames at 60 Hz), and writes schema-valid playtest_telemetry_v1 JSON to the requested path without crashing.

How it is automatable:

godot --headless --path <project-root> --fixed-fps 60 -- \
  --telemetry-out /tmp/hungerhall_smoke.json --games 200 --seed 1 --frame-budget 36000

The process must exit 0. The telemetry file must exist, be valid JSON, contain schema: "playtest_telemetry_v1", engine: "godot", engine_version matching Engine.get_version_info().string, games_played ≥ 20, and at least one level with plays > 0. A crash, missing file, invalid JSON, or missing required keys is a FAIL.

Pass condition: Process exits 0. Telemetry file exists and is schema-valid. games_played ≥ 20. At least one level has plays > 0. engine_version is not hardcoded (matches runtime).

GDD §10 open questions — test cross-reference (binding)

If any §10 question has no corresponding test, the prototype is DECORATIVE. The table in §6.4 is the binding cross-reference. Summary:

Q5: Continue economy fairnesstest_continue_reset.gd + test_death_penalty.gd + bot telemetry✓ Covered

Target telemetry bands explained:

  • win_rate: [0.30, 0.75] — the minimum-skill bot should clear floors 30–75% of the time. Below 30% indicates the floor is too hard for the stated combat estimates (G2 §3 provisional values). Above 75% indicates the floor is too easy. Human players should outperform the bot, so these bands are bot-calibrated, not human-calibrated.
  • dead_board_rate: [0.0, 0.05] — soft-locks should be 0 (solver guarantees), but the band allows 5% for edge cases the solver missed. Any non-zero dead_boards is flagged for investigation.
  • avg_floor_time_ticks_ratio: [0.40, 1.50] — the bot's average floor completion time as a ratio of the G2 §3 target midpoint (in ticks). Below 0.40 means the floor is trivially fast (too easy). Above 1.50 means the bot is taking 50% longer than target (too hard for minimum-skill agent — acceptable if human players can meet the target, but flagged for review).

Constants not worth machine-tuning (stay in code):

  • Tile size (32px) — structural constant, not a feel knob
  • Virtual resolution (640×360) — rendering constant
  • Physics tick rate (60 Hz) — determinism constant
  • Save schema version (1) — data format constant
  • Replay format fields — serialization constant
  • String keys — identity constant per G3
  • Palette hex values — art direction constant per G4
  • Class names (WARRIOR, VALKYRIE, WIZARD, ELF) — identity constant
  • Zone names — identity constant per G3

10. Asset placeholder strategy

The primary journey visibly consumes every qualified Forge asset it declares through Godot's real scene/resource path. A generated sprite sheet is consumed as a SpriteFrames animation with its declared frame geometry — it is not reduced to one crop.

Defensive fallback for missing primary-journey assets:

If a required primary-journey asset's file/import/binding is temporarily unavailable, the scene preserves playability with a defensive engine-native fallback:

  • Missing sprite: Godot ColorRect or Polygon2D in the palette slot for that entity's role token (e.g., hero_warrior #C87040 rectangle with silhouette-accurate proportions for a missing Warrior sprite). The fallback is intentionally unmistakable as a placeholder — a flat colored rectangle, not a fake sprite.
  • Missing tileset: Godot TileMap with ColorRect-colored cells (floor_mid for walkable, wall_body for walls, wall_cap for wall tops). Zone accent color applied as a tint.
  • Missing font: Godot default monospace font at the declared size — visibly different from Silkscreen, unmistakably a fallback.

Using any fallback records non-zero delivery_debt in the scene-binding receipt, names the slot, and sends the current playable build through the next automatic art/binding repair pass. The build is not called complete, polished, or visually qualified in this state. A required primary-journey slot is NOT an optional gap.

Optional gaps (fallback is acceptable, no delivery_debt):

  • Attract replay file (res://Assets/Replays/attract.replay) — the title screen may use a static title card or a live deterministic bot simulation instead. The replay playback code is implemented; the recorded file is not shipped in the prototype.
  • NG+ second baked floor set — NG+ parameter application on the 6 shipped floors is IN; a separately seeded floor set is OUT.
  • Credits scroll content — may use G3 credits copy as placeholder text (this is real copy from the voice bible, not Lorem Ipsum).
  • Announcer .wav clips — missing audio is NOT gameplay failure per §7.4. No-op hooks fire; captions still display (text is available from strings.json). The game is fully completable with audio muted (G2 §8.5).

Adversary checks — explicitly forbidden:

  • NO Lorem Ipsum text anywhere in the project.
  • NO Pixar-3D renders or 3D mesh claims (this is a pure 2D game per G1/G2).
  • NO copyrighted images (no Atari/Gauntlet assets, no borrowed sprites, no trademarked controller symbols — input glyphs are generic 1-bit geometry per G4).
  • NO fake provenance on any asset.
  • NO .godot/imported fabrication — all assets loaded through ResourceLoader at res:// paths or referenced by scene/script/resource.
  • A fallback is evidence debt, not the aesthetic target. The aesthetic target is governed art consumed through the engine's real resource system.
The frozen specificationwhat the argument left standing

HUNGERHALL — G6 Prototype Spec (Locked Runtime: Godot 4.7)

Run: gap-253b64a1 · Phase: G6 · Authority chain: G1 Concept Lock (FROZEN) → G2 GDD (FROZEN) → G3 Voice Bible (FROZEN) → G4 Art Direction (FROZEN, Palette A — "After Service") → G5 UX Flow (FROZEN, LAR-1–4 adopted) · Engine: Godot 4.7 (LOCKED — G7 does not relitigate) · Platform: Steam, Windows export — qualified as its own later lane, never claimed here · Price: $5.99 premium, zero post-purchase spending · Scope: commercial_focused

This document is the binding contract G7 reads as authoritative. Every file, test, scope boundary, and pin below is law. G7 reviewers reject code that drifts from this specification.

Novelty thesis. HUNGERHALL's HP drain is Gauntlet's drain, acknowledged. The four class names (Warrior, Valkyrie, Wizard, Elf) are also Gauntlet's roster, acknowledged. The mechanical fork is structural: a single-player finite campaign where four classes pay the same HP bill in different risk currencies, floors are solver-gated for structural solvability at bake time, and there are no in-run upgrades, no coin-op continue economy, and no item synergy drafting. Class distinctness is verified mechanically — no two classes share the same combat signature tuple (hp, speed, shot_dmg, shot_range, shot_rate, potion_type) — AND measured by dominance_spread_pp across bot policies, with an additional viability floor: min_class_win_rate ≥ 0.40 and min_class_avg_hp_at_exit ≥ 30. The novelty is the campaign structure and class-diversified risk economy, not the clock or the names.

G5 Lock-Amendment adoption: LAR-1 (ng_plus: bool in save, always false), LAR-2 (event-driven rumble patterns), LAR-3 (game_over → RetryChosen edge), LAR-4 (settings one flat column).

DIS position alignment: DIS-1 (SSM in app/, not core/) upheld. DIS-2 (tools/ present) upheld. DIS-3 (comprehensive Tunables) upheld. DIS-4 (all 10 modals) upheld. DIS-5 (replay playback, not live sim) — CHANGED: adopting replay-only position (meta/nvidia/deepseek-2); prior live-sim language removed throughout. DIS-6 (separate world/) upheld. DIS-7 (dedicated RulesCombat) upheld. DIS-8 (NG+ OUT) upheld. DIS-9 (step() name) upheld. DIS-10 (18 test suites) upheld.

1. Engine choice

Godot 4.7 is the locked runtime. No substitute may be proposed. RefCounted value types give the G2 §7 pure-rules contract a native home with zero Node/rendering/input coupling. The headless --fixed-fps 60 main-scene launch drives ci/sneferu_bot.gd against that same core for machine-graded telemetry. The locked 2D pixel presentation (32px tiles, 640×360 viewport, CanvasModulate, Control themes) maps directly to TileMap, CanvasLayer, SpriteFrames, and Theme resources. One ruleset serves player, bot, attract replay, and deterministic replay. Steam Windows export is a later qualification lane.

project.godot pins (binding on G7):

  • application/run/main_scene="res://main.tscn"
  • Exactly one autoload: SessionStateMachine → *res://app/session_state_machine.gd
  • physics/common/physics_ticks_per_second=60
  • rendering/textures/vram_compression/import_etc2_astc=true
  • renderer/rendering_method="gl_compatibility"
  • Window 1280×720, 640×360 base viewport, canvas_items stretch, keep aspect
  • Complete [input] map per §15

sneferu_primary_action resolution (all states): InputMapper resolves the Space binding contextually using SessionStateMachine.current_screen:

Current screenResolves as
Splashconfirm (skip to Title if ≥18 steps elapsed AND input received)
Titleconfirm (selects focused menu item)
ClassSelectconfirm (locks class, triggers DESCEND)
Playingthrow (fires projectile along facing)
Pausedresume (returns to Playing)
Settingsno-op (Settings uses its own input scheme)
HallOfHeroesback (returns to Title)
Dyingno-op (non-interactive)
ContinueOfferyes (selects YES continue)
GameOverconfirm (selects focused button)
FloorResultsadvance (proceeds to next floor)
CampaignResultsconfirm (commits initials, returns to Title)

This is an additional keyboard/accessibility binding riding the real controller path, never a test-only branch.

SessionStateMachine is the sole autoload. It does NOT declare class_name — the autoload name SessionStateMachine is the sole global accessor, avoiding class_name/autoload collision (OBL-55). It owns one RulesSession instance and state machine logic. It does NOT create scene nodes. main.gd is the sole composition root: it authors all app-layer nodes as children of Main in main.tscn, then wires them to SessionStateMachine via setter injection in _ready().

Adversary pre-emption. No Utils, Helpers, Common, or Misc directories. Every file has one responsibility. core/ imports nothing outside GDScript standard library. app/ imports core/ only. main.gd wires app-layer nodes to SSM via setters — SSM does NOT create scene nodes. scenes/ imports app/ (for ssm.request() verb calls) AND core/ (for snapshot Dictionaries + TunablesLoader). world/ imports core/ only. tests/ import core/ + app/ (NO tools/). tools/ imports core/ + data defs. Dependency direction: core/ ← app/ ← {ci/, tests/, scenes/}; core/ ← {scenes/, world/, ui/}. No module imports back from its caller.

3. Module boundaries

3.1 Enum definitions (state_enums.gd)
# State enum — 12 session states
enum State {
    SPLASH = 0, TITLE = 1, CLASS_SELECT = 2, PLAYING = 3,
    PAUSED = 4, SETTINGS = 5, HALL_OF_HEROES = 6,
    DYING = 7, CONTINUE_OFFER = 8, GAME_OVER = 9,
    FLOOR_RESULTS = 10, CAMPAIGN_RESULTS = 11
}

# SceneId enum — 22 scene identifiers (12 screens + 10 modals)
enum SceneId {
    SPLASH = 0, TITLE = 1, CLASS_SELECT = 2, PLAY = 3,
    PAUSED = 4, SETTINGS = 5, HALL_OF_HEROES = 6,
    DYING = 7, CONTINUE_OFFER = 8, GAME_OVER = 9,
    FLOOR_RESULTS = 10, CAMPAIGN_RESULTS = 11,
    MODAL_QUIT_WARN = 12, MODAL_NEWGAME_WARN = 13,
    MODAL_ERASE_WARN = 14, MODAL_RESET_WARN = 15,
    MODAL_REMAP_CAPTURE = 16, MODAL_CREDITS_POP = 17,
    MODAL_PRIVACY_POP = 18, MODAL_PAD_LOST = 19,
    MODAL_SAVE_FAIL = 20, MODAL_FLOOR_MISSING = 21
}

# Verb enum — 21 transition verbs
enum Verb {
    PRESS = 0, RESUME = 1, CHOOSE = 2, PAUSE = 3,
    QUIT = 4, CLEAR = 5, FINISH = 6, ADVANCE = 7,
    SAVE_QUIT = 8, ENTER = 9, DRAIN = 10, PROMPT = 11,
    CONTINUE = 12, EXPIRE = 13, BACK = 14, SETTINGS = 15,
    RETRY = 16, SKIP = 17, CONFIRM = 18, CANCEL = 19,
    TIMEOUT = 20
}

# ClassType enum — 4 classes
enum ClassType { WARRIOR = 0, VALKYRIE = 1, WIZARD = 2, ELF = 3 }

# EnemyAIType enum — 6 AI types
enum EnemyAIType {
    GHOST = 0, GRUNT = 1, DEMON = 2,
    LOBBER = 3, SORCERER = 4, DEATH = 5
}

# HazardType enum — 3 hazard types
enum HazardType { FLAME_JET = 0, VOID_BRIDGE = 1, COLLAPSING_VOID = 2 }

# TriggerType enum — 3 trigger types
enum TriggerType { PERIODIC = 0, PHASED = 1, PLAYER_STEP = 2 }

# PotionType enum — 4 class-specific potion effects
enum PotionType { WHIRLWIND = 0, AEGIS = 1, NOVA = 2, VOLLEY = 3 }

Class-to-potion mapping: Warrior→WHIRLWIND, Valkyrie→AEGIS, Wizard→NOVA, Elf→VOLLEY. Each class has a unique potion_type integer (0–3), ensuring the distinctness tuple (hp, speed, shot_dmg, shot_range, shot_rate, potion_type) is mechanically distinct for all four classes.

3.2 TransitionTable (complete entries with condition vocabulary)

Condition vocabulary (evaluated by SessionStateMachine before approving a transition):

Condition stringPredicate
"always"No precondition
"save_exists"SaveStore.read_campaign() returns valid data
"no_save"SaveStore.read_campaign() returns empty/invalid
"hp_zero"RulesSession.snapshot()["hp"] <= 0
"exit_overlap_3 AND floor_lt_24"_exit_overlap_count >= 3 AND current_floor < 24
"exit_overlap_3 AND floor_eq_24"_exit_overlap_count >= 3 AND current_floor == 24
"tokens_gt_0 AND yes"tokens > 0 AND continue_selection == YES
"no OR timeout OR tokens_eq_0"continue_selection == NO OR _continue_timer <= 0 OR tokens == 0
"dying_complete"_dying_step_count >= 72 (normal) or >= 12 (reduced motion)
"splash_complete_or_skippable"_splash_step_count >= 72 OR (input_received AND _splash_step_count >= 18)
"entered_from_paused"_settings_entry_screen == PAUSED
"entered_from_title"_settings_entry_screen == TITLE

3.3 pending_events schema

RulesSession.consume_pending() returns {cues: Array[Dictionary], events: Array[Dictionary]}. Each event Dictionary:

{
  "type": "StringName",     // e.g., "generator_destroyed", "player_hit", "floor_clear",
                            // "food_consumed", "key_collected", "potion_used",
                            // "door_opened", "chest_opened", "throw", "projectile_hit",
                            // "death", "zone_entry"
  "step": 42,               // int: step at which event occurred
  "position": [320, 224],   // Vector2 as [x, y] in world pixels
  "entity_id": 3,           // int: ID of affected entity (0=player, >0=enemy/gen/pickup)
  "amount": 150             // int: damage, score value, HP restore, etc. (0 if N/A)
}

Each cue Dictionary: {"cue_id": "StringName", "step": int}.

3.4 RulesSession internal composition

RulesSession (RefCounted) owns these internal fields, all initialized in setup_campaign():

FieldTypePurpose
_floorRulesFloorCurrent floor state (null when not PLAYING)
_playerRulesPlayerPlayer state: HP, position, facing, cooldowns, potions, keys
_enemiesArray[RulesEnemy]Active enemies on current floor
_generatorsArray[RulesGenerator]Active generators on current floor
_hazardsArray[RulesHazard]Active hazards on current floor
_projectilesArray[RulesProjectile]Active projectiles (player + enemy)
_pickupsRulesPickupPickup state manager: food, keys, potions, chests, doors
_scoreRulesScoreScore tracker: cumulative score, kills, death penalties
_tunablesTunablesLoaderLoaded tunables (passed in at construction)
_prngPrngSeederSession-level PRNG (for non-floor randomness)
_stateint (State enum)Current session state
_step_countintTotal steps since floor load
_killsintTotal kills this floor
_shots_firedintTotal shots this floor
_death_causeStringnull/"drain"/"contact"/"hazard"/"step_limit"
_pending_cuesArray[Dictionary]Buffered cues (drained by consume_pending)
_pending_eventsArray[Dictionary]Buffered events (drained by consume_pending)
_exit_overlap_countintConsecutive frames of exit overlap
_class_typeint (ClassType enum)Locked class for this campaign
_campaign_seedintSeed for this campaign
_current_floorintCurrent floor index (1-based)
_tokensintContinue tokens remaining
_potionsintPotion inventory
_keysintKey inventory

step() delegates to: _player.update(_tunables) (drain, cooldowns) → _enemies AI → _generators spawn check → _hazards update → _projectiles move/collide → RulesCombat.resolve() → _pickups overlap → RulesScore.update() → _check_transitions(). Each sub-system appends to _pending_cues and _pending_events.

3.5 core/ — Pure deterministic simulation
  • Types: RulesSession, TransitionTable, RulesFloor, RulesPlayer, RulesEnemy, RulesGenerator, RulesHazard, RulesProjectile, RulesCombat (static), RulesScore, RulesPickup, RulesContinue, RulesReplay, RulesSolverCheck (static), SaveCodec, TunablesLoader, PrngSeeder, Resource subclasses, StateEnums. All RefCounted or Resource.
  • IS responsible for: The whole deterministic truth of a run at fixed 60 Hz. HP, score, spawns, hazards, damage, transition legality (data table), combat, scoring, continue/respawn, save encode/decode, replay serialization, tunables parsing, solver gate verification, resource definitions. Owns seeded PRNG via RulesFloor. Produces pending_cues and pending_events arrays in snapshot.
  • IS NOT responsible for: Pixels, input polling, audio playback, disk writes, scene management, UI rendering, CueBus dispatch.
  • Public API: — RulesSession.setup_campaign(seed: int, class_type: int, tunables: TunablesLoader) → void — RulesSession.load_floor(floor_index: int) → void — loads baked FloorData; resets tokens to tokens_per_floor — RulesSession.continue_floor() → void — decrements tokens by 1; rebuilds current floor; HP=50% max; potions=0; keys=0; food NOT restored; generators full — RulesSession.retry_floor() → void — resets tokens to tokens_per_floor; rebuilds current floor; HP=class max; potions=0; keys=0 — RulesSession.input(action: Dictionary) → void — action = {move: Vector2, attack: bool, potion: bool}; NO pause field — RulesSession.step() → void — no delta parameter; one step = 1/60s; only called by SSM when current_screen == PLAYING — RulesSession.snapshot() → Dictionary — includes: state, hp, score, floor, position, facing, enemies, generators, tokens, potions, keys, food_positions, key_positions, door_positions, exit_position, hazards, projectiles, step_count, kills, shots_fired, death_cause, pending_cues, pending_events. Does NOT clear pending arrays. — RulesSession.consume_pending() → Dictionary — returns {cues: Array, events: Array} and clears both internal buffers (destructive read) — RulesSession.has_legal_action() → bool — returns true if ANY of: (a) move in any of 8 directions where destination tile is not WALL/locked-door, (b) throw if _player.shot_cooldown_steps <= 0, (c) potion if _player.potions > 0. Used by softlock detection. — RulesSession.step_count → int (read-only) — RulesSession.kills → int (read-only) — RulesSession.shots_fired → int (read-only) — RulesSession.death_cause → String (read-only: null/"drain"/"contact"/"hazard"/"step_limit") — TunablesLoader.get(name: String) → Variant — SaveCodec.encode(dict) → String; SaveCodec.decode(json) → Dictionary (returns {success, data, needs_migration_notice}) — RulesSolverCheck.verify_floor(floor_data: FloorData, tunables: TunablesLoader) → Dictionary (returns {passed: bool, failed_gates: Array[String]}) — RulesReplay.hash_snapshot(snapshot: Dictionary) → String — SHA-256 via HashingContext with HASHING_ALGORITHM_SHA256 over canonical JSON (keys sorted alphabetically, no whitespace, non-JSON-native types converted: Vector2 → [x, y], Color → [r, g, b, a], StringName → String, enum → int)
  • Imports: Nothing outside core/.
3.6 app/ — Controller layer
  • Types: SessionStateMachine (sole autoload, NO class_name), SceneRouter, InputMapper, SaveStore, ProfileStore, ScoreStore, SettingsStore, Announcer, CueBus, AudioDirector, JuiceDirector.
  • IS responsible for: Translation between engine reality and core. Flow relay. Save writing (campaign, profile, scores, settings — each on its own atomic path). Cue dispatch. Bark queue. Juice direction. Procedural audio gap cues. Rumble emission. Freeze-frame counter (SSM-internal).
  • IS NOT responsible for: Damage math, spawn logic, layout decisions, transition legality (data table in core/), rendering, direct scene script imports.
  • Public API (SessionStateMachine): — set_scene_router(router: SceneRouter) → void — set_cue_bus(bus: CueBus) → void — set_audio_director(director: AudioDirector) → void — set_juice_director(director: JuiceDirector) → void — set_input_mapper(mapper: InputMapper) → void — set_save_store(store: SaveStore) → void — set_profile_store(store: ProfileStore) → void — set_score_store(store: ScoreStore) → void — set_settings_store(store: SettingsStore) → void — set_announcer(announcer: Announcer) → void — request(verb: StringName, params := {}) → void — current_screen → int (read-only; returns State enum value) — set_campaign_seed(seed: int) → void — tick_once() → void — public test API: performs one SSM internal step (process timers, advance rules if PLAYING, check transitions, dispatch cues/events). _physics_process(delta) calls tick_once() in production. Tests call tick_once() directly without a running SceneTree. — freeze_steps_remaining → int (internal counter; when > 0, step() is skipped and counter decremented)
  • Public API (SceneRouter): @export var scene_map: Dictionary (SceneId enum → PackedScene); mount(scene_id: int) → void; hide(scene_id: int) → void; current_scene_id → int (read-only); get_active_scene() → Node — returns the currently mounted screen Node or null
  • Public API (CueBus): emit(cue_id: StringName, params := {}) → void; emitted_log: Array[Dictionary]
  • Public API (SaveStore): write_campaign(data: Dictionary) → bool; write_profile(data: Dictionary) → bool; write_scores(data: Dictionary) → bool; write_settings(data: Dictionary) → bool; read_campaign() → Dictionary; read_profile() → Dictionary; read_scores() → Dictionary; read_settings() → Dictionary; erase_all() → bool; erase_settings() → bool
  • Public API (JuiceDirector): trigger_freeze(steps: int) → void (sets ssm.freeze_steps_remaining); rumble(pattern: String, intensity: float) → void (scales by settings.rumble_intensity; 0 = off); set_settings_store(store: SettingsStore) → void (for rumble scaling)
  • Public API (AudioDirector): play_cue(cue_id: StringName) → void (scales volume by settings.sfx_vol / 100.0; sfx_vol = 0 silences)
  • Imports: core/ only.
3.7 scenes/ — Thin projections
  • Types: One .tscn + .gd pair per screen and modal (12 screens, 10 modals).
  • IS responsible for: Snapshot → pixels and intent → SessionStateMachine.request(...). play.gd exposes consume_events(events: Array) → void which forwards events to WorldView.consume_events(). title.gd MUST load res://Assets/Replays/attract.replay and drive an isolated RulesSession from recorded actions at 30Hz — this attract session is isolated from the game session and drives only the AttractViewport's inner WorldView. The "MAY" from prior drafts is replaced with "MUST."
  • IS NOT responsible for: A second truth store, rules engine, direct caller of other screens, save logic.
  • Imports: app/ (for ssm.request() verb calls), core/ snapshot Dictionaries (read-only), core/ TunablesLoader. title.gd also imports core/ RulesSession + RulesReplay for attract playback (explicitly required).
3.8 world/ — World projection
  • Types: WorldView, ActorSprites, CameraRig, LifeLight, Particles, Floaters.
  • IS responsible for: Node2D dressing of Play snapshot. WorldView.consume_events(events) processes pending_events for visual juice (particles, floaters, trauma). Reads juice constants from TunablesLoader.
  • IS NOT responsible for: Game state, AI, timing authority, CueBus dispatch, direct app/ calls.
  • Imports: core/ snapshot Dictionaries and core/ TunablesLoader only.
3.9 ui/ — Themed Control widgets
  • Types: Theme, StyleBox, HUD, caption band, continue ring, initials, idle prompts, guestbook, glyphs.
  • Imports: core/ TunablesLoader (for caption timing only).
3.10 data/, tools/, ci/, tests/
  • data/: Baked resources + JSON manifests. strings.json categories: "bark", "caption", "ui", "credits", "privacy". Accessed via ResourceLoader.load("res://data/...") or FileAccess.open("res://data/...").
  • tools/: FloorBaker (requires --seed <int>), Solver (calls core/rules_solver_check.gd; --check-band-extremes flag), AttractCapture (bakes attract.replay). Imports core/ + data defs.
  • ci/: SneferuBot (RefCounted, invoked by main.gd). Public API: SneferuBot.run(session: RulesSession, policy: String, telemetry_path: String, games: int, seed: int, frame_budget: int) → void. CLI args via OS.get_cmdline_user_args(): --telemetry-out <abs> --games <int> --seed <int> --frame-budget <int> --policy <string>. Invalid args → stderr error + exit code 2, no telemetry written. Game crashes caught and recorded in errors[]. Architecture skill waiver documented in §2 layout.
  • tests/: 19 test modules + test_runner.gd. Runs without autoloads. SSM-dependent tests instantiate SessionStateMachine as a regular Node with mock dependencies and call tick_once() directly.

4. State management approach

1. Pure simulation Core. All game logic lives in core/ RefCounted objects with no Node, Control, Viewport, Input, AudioStream, or frame-rate dependency. RulesSession is the single entry point. Input arrives as semantic actions: {move: Vector2, attack: bool, potion: bool} — pause is an app-level verb. The core advances one fixed step per RulesSession.step() call (no delta parameter; one step = 1/60s). All randomness flows from RulesFloor's seeded RandomNumberGenerator initialized via PrngSeeder.from_int(seed).

Seed hierarchy:

  • Campaign seed: bot/journey receives --seed; player campaign seed = Time.get_ticks_msec() at ClassSelect→Playing (stored in save). main.gd reads --seed or --journey-seed from OS.get_cmdline_user_args() if present and calls ssm.set_campaign_seed(seed).
  • Floor seed: campaign_seed XOR (floor_index * 0x1000) — deterministic per floor, same across continue/retry.
  • Balance sim per-game seed: game_seed = campaign_seed + game_id; floor seed derived as above. Pinned for deterministic reproducibility.
  • Attract: seed 0xDEAD (57005) frozen in attract.replay at bake time — NOT a tunable.

Snapshot + drain semantics: RulesSession.snapshot() returns a read-only Dictionary including pending_cues and pending_events but does NOT clear them. RulesSession.consume_pending() → Dictionary performs a destructive read. SessionStateMachine calls snapshot() for state, then consume_pending() for events/cues, dispatching cues to CueBus and events to the active screen's consume_events() via SceneRouter.get_active_scene().

2. Application/controller layer. SessionStateMachine (single autoload, NO class_name) owns the 12 session states. It does NOT create scene nodes. main.gd is the composition root: in _ready(), it gets @onready references to all app-layer children of Main and calls ssm.set_*() for each. The SSM then: derives semantic actions from InputMap via InputMapper, calls RulesSession.input(...), advances core via tick_once(), reads snapshot + consume_pending(), dispatches to CueBus/JuiceDirector/active scene, and approves transitions via TransitionTable. This layer contains no rules.

tick_once() — the injectable clock (OBL-2/OBL-39/OBL-63/OBL-82):

func tick_once() -> void:
    # 1. Process step-counted timers (splash, dying, continue_offer)
    _process_timers()
    # 2. Check joypad disconnect (pad_lost trigger)
    _check_joypad()
    # 3. Advance rules ONLY when current_screen == PLAYING
    if current_screen == State.PLAYING and _freeze_steps_remaining <= 0:
        _rules.input(_pending_action)
        _rules.step()
    elif _freeze_steps_remaining > 0:
        _freeze_steps_remaining -= 1  # clock pauses during freeze
    # 4. Read snapshot + consume_pending
    _last_snapshot = _rules.snapshot()
    var pending = _rules.consume_pending()
    # 5. Dispatch cues to CueBus
    for cue in pending.cues:
        _cue_bus.emit(cue.cue_id)
    # 6. Dispatch events to JuiceDirector (rumble) + active scene
    _juice_director.process_events(pending.events)
    var active = _scene_router.get_active_scene()
    if active and active.has_method("consume_events"):
        active.consume_events(pending.events)
    # 7. Check transitions
    _check_transitions()

In production, _physics_process(delta) calls tick_once(). In tests, test_runner.gd calls ssm.tick_once() directly — no SceneTree required.

Step advancement invariant (OBL-49/OBL-62): RulesSession.step() is called ONLY when current_screen == PLAYING AND _freeze_steps_remaining == 0. All other states (Paused, Dying, ContinueOffer, FloorResults, GameOver, CampaignResults, Settings, HallOfHeroes, Title, Splash, ClassSelect) do NOT advance the simulation. Step-counted timers (splash, dying, continue_offer) are SSM-internal counters advanced in _process_timers() regardless of rules advancement.

Freeze-frame mechanism (OBL-8/OBL-25/OBL-56/OBL-63/OBL-86): The freeze is an SSM-internal counter, not a reverse signal from JuiceDirector. When SSM processes events from consume_pending() and encounters a freeze-triggering event (generator_destroyed, player_hit), it sets _freeze_steps_remaining = round(tunables.juice_freeze_frame_s * 60). While _freeze_steps_remaining > 0, step() is not called — the simulation clock pauses (corrected from prior "unaffected" wording). The counter decrements each tick_once(). JuiceDirector handles ONLY rumble and visual juice (particles, trauma) — it does NOT signal SSM to freeze. One direction: SSM reads events → SSM sets counter. JuiceDirector.trigger_freeze(steps) is retained as a convenience API that sets ssm.freeze_steps_remaining directly, called by SSM itself (not by scenes).

Under reduced motion (OBL-22/OBL-76): _freeze_steps_remaining is always 0 — freeze-frames are fully disabled, satisfying GDD Q10's "disable freeze-frames." Screenshake amplitude is 0. Vignette replaces hit flash.

Continue token accounting (OBL-18/OBL-66):

  • load_floor(): tokens reset to tokens_per_floor (2) at each floor entry (ClassSelect→Playing and FloorResults→Advance)
  • continue_floor(): tokens -= 1; floor rebuilt from baked data; HP = 50% class max; potions = 0; keys = 0; food stays consumed; generators reset to full
  • retry_floor(): tokens reset to tokens_per_floor (2); floor rebuilt; HP = class max; potions = 0; keys = 0
  • When tokens == 0 at ContinueOffer entry: auto-expire after 120 steps (no input needed)

3. Thin projection. Screens and world view read the snapshot and render. WorldView.consume_events() processes pending_events for visual juice. play.gd.consume_events(events) forwards events to WorldView. A scene is never a second truth store.

4. Navigation owner. SceneRouter (child of Main) manages screen visibility. @export scene_map: Dictionary maps SceneId enum values to PackedScene resources, authored in the editor. TransitionTable in core/ is the single legality authority. SessionStateMachine checks the table and calls router.mount(scene_id) / router.hide(scene_id). SceneRouter.get_active_scene() returns the currently mounted Node for event dispatch.

Input buffering justification (OBL-3): Zero input buffering is a deliberate design choice. The fixed 60 Hz physics step means maximum input latency is 1 frame (16.67 ms), well under the 100 ms acknowledgment threshold. Throw and potion are discrete actions fired on press frame, not held. Movement is a continuous 8-way vector read each physics frame. A buffer would add complexity without reducing effective latency at 60 Hz.

Pause process-mode contract (OBL-19/OBL-20/OBL-21/OBL-62): Uses exact Godot 4.7 ProcessMode constants:

NodeProcess modeRationale
SessionStateMachine (autoload)PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYSMust detect pause input, manage state, run timers
Main (main.gd)PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYSBot-mode lifecycle, wiring
SceneRouterPROCESS_MODE_ALWAYSMust mount/hide screens during pause
InputMapperPROCESS_MODE_ALWAYSMust read pause/confirm/joypad disconnect
CueBusPROCESS_MODE_ALWAYSMust dispatch cues during BOTH paused and unpaused
AudioDirectorPROCESS_MODE_ALWAYSMust play audio during BOTH paused and unpaused
AnnouncerPROCESS_MODE_ALWAYSCaptions during BOTH paused and unpaused
JuiceDirectorPROCESS_MODE_PAUSABLEJuice stops during pause
SaveStore/ProfileStore/ScoreStore/SettingsStorePROCESS_MODE_ALWAYSMust save at any time
Splash, Title screensPROCESS_MODE_ALWAYSTitle/attract never paused
Play (WorldView, HUD, CaptionBand)PROCESS_MODE_PAUSABLEGame stops during pause
Paused screenPROCESS_MODE_ALWAYSActive during pause
Settings (context-dependent)SSM sets PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS if entered from Title; PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS if from Paused (settings must remain interactive in both contexts)
HallOfHeroes, Dying, ContinueOffer, GameOver, FloorResults, CampaignResultsPROCESS_MODE_PAUSABLENot reachable during pause; SSM controls visibility
All modalsPROCESS_MODE_ALWAYSModals appear in both paused and unpaused contexts; SSM controls visibility and tree pause state

Pause mechanism: SSM sets get_tree().paused = true on entering Paused; false on exit. tick_once() skips RulesSession.step() when current_screen != PLAYING.

Why this split serves THIS prototype: The same RulesSession path is exercised by player, replay, attract, and bot. Determinism, balance, and replay regression are one testable surface. Godot scenes only project state; the controller only relays intent.

AttractViewport pin (OBL-58): SubViewport size 320×224 pixels. Inner Camera2D with zoom = Vector2(2, 2). AttractWorldView at 0.5× scale relative to gameplay WorldView. No audio bus routing. Looping playback; no live simulation.

Attract mode contract (OBL-1/OBL-26/OBL-71/OBL-77): title.gd MUST load res://Assets/Replays/attract.replay (schema hungerhall_replay_v1, seed 0xDEAD, Warrior, floor 1). It creates an isolated RulesSession, calls setup_campaign(0xDEAD, ClassType.WARRIOR, _tunables), load_floor(1), then applies recorded actions from the replay file at 30 Hz (every 2nd physics frame). pending_cues are suppressed (not dispatched to CueBus). The session loops by resetting to action[0] when the action list is exhausted. No live simulation, no live AI, no live bot — pure replay playback. attract.replay is produced by tools/attract_capture.gd at build time.

Cross-reference G5 screen graph: Splash, Title, ClassSelect, Play, Paused, Settings, HallOfHeroes, Dying, ContinueOffer, GameOver, FloorResults, CampaignResults — all 12 G5 screens present. All 10 G5 modals present. Title menu rows include Continue (with disabled state when no save exists), enabling the Title→Resume→Playing transition.

Event dispatch path (OBL-9/OBL-57/OBL-66): SSM tick_once() → consume_pending() → SceneRouter.get_active_scene() → if active scene has consume_events(events), call it → play.gd.consume_events() → WorldView.consume_events(). This is the sole event dispatch path from core to presentation.

6.3 GODOT PLAYTEST CONTRACT

The configured main scene recognizes bot arguments after -- and invokes ci/sneferu_bot.gd (RefCounted class) against the same RulesSession core. Telemetry written atomically (temp-file + rename) to --telemetry-out.

Pinned command (Criterion 3 — smoke, single-policy 200-game):

godot --headless --path <project-root> --fixed-fps 60 -- \
  --telemetry-out <absolute-path> --games 200 --seed 1 --frame-budget 21600 --policy greedy-killer

--frame-budget 21600 = max steps per single floor attempt (one bot "game" = one floor attempt). 21,600 steps = 360 seconds at 60 Hz. --policy = one of greedy-killer, speed-runner, survival-router. Three separate runs (one per policy) are the only path for Criterion 2 aggregate metrics.

CI wall-clock budget (OBL-54): 200 games × max 21,600 steps = max 4,320,000 steps. At --fixed-fps 60 headless fast-forward (no rendering, no vsync), typical throughput is ≥100,000 steps/sec. Expected wall-clock: ≤ 90 seconds per run. Total for all three Criterion 2 runs: ≤ 5 minutes.

Telemetry schema for Criterion 3 (playtest_telemetry_v1 — single-policy, 200 games):

{
  "schema": "playtest_telemetry_v1",
  "engine_version": "4.7",
  "project_hash": "<SHA-256 per §16 algorithm>",
  "policy": "greedy-killer",
  "games_played": 200,
  "games_completed": 200,
  "per_game": [{"game_id": 0, "class": "warrior", "floor": 1, "policy": "greedy-killer",
    "seed": 2, "outcome": "win", "steps_used": 3600, "step_limit": 21600,
    "hp_at_exit": 450, "kills": 12, "shots_fired": 48, "death_cause": null}],
  "levels": [{"level_id": 1, "plays": 9, "wins": 7, "avg_steps_used": 3600,
    "step_limit": 21600, "dead_boards": 0}],
  "totals": {"win_rate": 0.72, "dead_board_rate": 0.04,
    "per_class_win_rate": {"warrior": 0.74, "valkyrie": 0.70, "wizard": 0.68, "elf": 0.76},
    "wizard_avg_hp_at_exit": 85},
  "errors": [],
  "notes": []
}

outcome enumerated values (OBL-15/OBL-43): "win" (floor cleared via exit door), "death" (HP reached zero), "step_limit" (max steps reached without clearing or dying).

dead_board_rate for Criterion 3 (OBL-17/OBL-89): Denominator = 24 floor-policy pairs (24 floors × 1 policy). A "dead board" = floor where zero wins occurred. Rate = dead_boards / 24.

games_completed = number of games that reached a terminal state (win, death, or step_limit) without crashing. Must equal games_played for Criterion 3 to pass. errors[]: any entry fails Criterion 3 — zero errors required.

    "per_class_win_rate": {"warrior": 0.74, "valkyrie": 0.70, "wizard": 0.68, "elf": 0.76},
    "min_class_win_rate": 0.68,
    "min_class_avg_hp_at_exit": 62,
    "softlock_count": 0
  },
  "per_policy": [
    {"policy": "greedy-killer", "win_rate": 0.74, "dead_board_rate": 0.04},
    {"policy": "speed-runner", "win_rate": 0.69, "dead_board_rate": 0.02},
    {"policy": "survival-router", "win_rate": 0.73, "dead_board_rate": 0.03}
  ],
  "errors": []
}

dead_board_rate for Criterion 2 (OBL-50/OBL-67): Denominator = 72 floor-policy pairs (24 floors × 3 policies). Rate = dead_boards / 72.

dominance_spread_pp (OBL-50): (max_class_win_rate — min_class_win_rate) × 100, computed across all 600 games. Criterion 2 requires ≤ 30.

wizard_avg_hp_at_exit: Average HP at exit across Wizard wins only. If zero Wizard wins occur across all 600 games, Criterion 2 FAILS.

Novelty acceptance thresholds (OBL-91): Beyond tuple inequality: dominance_spread_pp ≤ 30, min_class_win_rate ≥ 0.40, min_class_avg_hp_at_exit ≥ 30. These verify class distinctness translates to viable, balanced gameplay.
